543066|2026-06.headline: SBI Cards Q1 FY27 PAT rose 20% YoY to INR664 crores on a sharp fall in credit cost to 6.5% gross, while revenue grew only 3%.
543066|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 profit grew on lower credit costs rather than revenue, with total revenue of INR5,205 crores up 3% YoY and gross credit cost down 301 bps YoY to 6.5%. Card spends hit a record INR1,18,475 crores (up 27% YoY) and spend market share rose to 19.5%, but receivables grew only about 2% QoQ and 3% YoY to INR58,269 crores. Management said asset growth should pick up from H2 FY27 and that cost of funds, stable at 6.6% this quarter, is expected to trend higher. Gross NPA fell to 2.04% and net NPA to 0.83%, the lowest since Q3 FY23.

segments.name: Retail cards
segments.commentary: Retail spends INR94,033 crores, up 14% YoY; online contributed 63% of retail spend and UPI on credit card usage grew 13% QoQ. Interest-earning assets stable at about 55%, revolver rate 22%.

segments.name: Corporate cards
segments.commentary: Corporate spend share was 20.33% of total spend this quarter, down from 21.92% last quarter; management targets about 20% and says corporate card profitability is very low.

segments.name: EMI / instalment lending
segments.commentary: EMI book stated at about 33% of portfolio per analyst question; management gave no numerical guidance but expects an uptick in festive season.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term ROA guidance of 4% to 4.5% reiterated; management says current trajectory (3.9% in Q1) puts it on track.
Gross credit cost expected to stay within the current range, subject to Middle East conflict impact; no numerical guidance given, but moderation expected.
Asset growth expected to pick up from H2 FY27 on higher acquisitions and festive season in Q3.
Cost of funds expected to trend higher in line with market rates; management also said cost of funds should remain in a similar range near term and depends on T-bill rates.
FY27 cost-to-income ratio expected in the range of about 56% to 58% (annual average).
NIM expected to stay around current levels (10.8%); revolver rates expected to stay stable.
Overlay of INR70 crores retained in Stage 1 for geopolitical uncertainty; INR65 crores released on improved portfolio mix.
Instalment-based (instance) fee income expected to rise in H2 on base effect; late fee income to stay at current level.
capex_capacity: Cards in force about 2.26 crores, up 7% YoY; more than 1 million new accounts added in Q1 FY27 (+17% YoY); net card addition of 4.84 lakh, highest in industry for the quarter per RBI data.
Sourcing split about 47% Banca and 53% open market.
Annual ECL model review completed in Q1: INR180 crores of the INR220 crores overlay consumed, INR65 crores released; INR70 crores overlay retained in Stage 1.
Write-back of INR35 crores on account of good asset quality this quarter, per management presentation.
Capital adequacy ratio 25.6%; liquidity described as strong.
demand_pricing: Spend market share rose to 19.5% (RBI June 2026 data) from 18.1% in FY26; market share in cards in force is 18.6%.
Strong spend categories: consumer durables, furnishing and hardware, apparel and jewellery; UPI on credit card growing with RuPay and QR acceptance.
Management says retail spending remains strong into Q2 despite monsoon concerns; festive season still ahead.
Rental transactions reopened only where acquirers have KYC'd landlords; volumes minimal and management is not pursuing rental fee income.
Management noted entry rates into the first delinquency bucket are near decadal lows.
Analyst cited a competitor expecting credit cost near 5% by Q3; management declined to endorse normalisation levels, saying moderation will continue.
Personal loans on credit card: management said it is not currently offering PL to new customers and is internally evaluating it.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for revolver trend and EMI share growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Revolver rates expected to stay stable in a similar range after a slight downward bias; no numerical guidance on EMI share, but an uptick expected with festive season.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company offer personal loans via cards and how is the EMI share being raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Some existing customers carry PL assets, but new PL offering is paused; the company is evaluating it internally. EMI push relies on pay-in-EMI in the app, OEM and PG tie-ups, and a rise in durables prices.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost guidance for exit of FY27 and receivables growth?
qa_highlights.answer: No numerical guidance; credit cost expected to moderate further and receivables to grow in H2 FY27. Management declined to give absolute or percentage numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Relative economics of retail vs corporate spends?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate spends targeted at around 20% (industry 20-25%); corporate cards have no lending, earn only interchange and fees, and have very low profitability versus retail.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the QoQ rise in employee opex?
qa_highlights.answer: Increase due to higher past service cost provision from the new wage code liability.

qa_highlights.question: Can yields be held or improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Yields to be kept in a broad range; levers include higher credit lines for instalment customers, and cost of funds increases pass through to incremental book.

qa_highlights.question: Will ECL model refresh give tailwind next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Model will not be relaxed; any gains come from data refresh as asset quality improves, with ECL release already occurring.

qa_highlights.question: Stress in IT/salaried segments in South India?
qa_highlights.answer: No cohort stress seen in the book, including separate IT-sector analysis; monitoring continues despite reports of higher delinquencies at other lenders.

qa_highlights.question: Cost-to-income outlook for full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year cost-to-income expected at about 56% to 58% as an average of four quarters; festive quarter will be higher.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook given rate pause?
qa_highlights.answer: NIM expected to stay around current levels; cost of funds managed through source and pricing choices.

risks_watch: Cost of funds expected to rise with market rates, pressuring NIM from 10.8% if yields do not keep pace.
Middle East conflict and fuel price/inflation second-order effects on customer cash flows; management says no substantial impact seen yet.
Receivables growth only 3% YoY; growth recovery is guided to H2 FY27 and depends on acquisition quality and festive season.
Competitive pressure from NBFC consumer-durable loans and personal loans cannibalising card EMI and spend.
Opex rising QoQ with festive season; cost-to-income guided at 56-58% for FY27.
Monsoon impact on retail spend and whether the INR70 crore Stage 1 overlay is released.

rows.why: Full-year cost-to-income is guided at 56-58% with the festive quarter explicitly running higher, and Q1 opex already rose QoQ on a wage-code past service cost provision.

543066|2026-09.headline: SBI Card Q2 FY27 PAT rose 75% YoY to INR778 crore on lower credit costs, while spend growth was just 3% and NIM is guided range-bound around 10.8%.
543066|2026-09.overview: SBI Card reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of INR5,141 crore (up 4% YoY) and PAT of INR778 crore (up 75% YoY), driven mainly by lower credit costs. Gross credit cost fell to 5.6% (down 98 bps QoQ and 342 bps YoY) and gross NPA to 1.9%. Total spends grew about 3% YoY to INR1,10,689 crore, with retail spends up 6% to a record INR95,299 crore, and management attributed the weak headline to festive timing shifting into Q3. Management expects receivables to grow from Q3 and retail spend growth of mid-teens to high-teens for FY27, but gave no receivables growth guidance. NIM was 10.8% with cost of funds up 18 bps QoQ to 6.8%, and management expects NIM to be range-bound as rate hikes feed in.

financial_highlights.metric: Daily weighted average cost of funds

segments.name: Retail spends
segments.commentary: Record INR95,299 crore in Q2, up 6% YoY; online was 62.8% of retail spend in H1 FY27. UPI spends on credit cards grew 17% QoQ, with INR21,300 crore of spends through UPI this quarter.

segments.name: Corporate spends
segments.commentary: INR15,390 crore in Q2, down QoQ; management says corporate is opportunistic, kept below 20% of total spend, and some spends were let go for margin reasons.

segments.name: Cards in force and acquisition
segments.commentary: Cards in force about 2 crore (32 lakh), up 8% YoY; more than 1 million new accounts added in Q2, up 18% YoY, with 49% from Banca and 51% from open market. Net addition of 8.6 lakh cards in FY27 to August.

guidance_outlook: Retail spend growth expected in the mid-teens to high-teens range for FY27 (management referenced a 14-16% range).
Receivables growth expected to start in H2 FY27 and from Q3; no numerical receivables growth guidance given.
NIM expected to be range-bound; cost of funds expected to rise over the next few quarters, with a possible further ~50 bps repo hike, impact expected to lag as the book reprices in about 60-75 days.
Gross credit cost expected around 6% for FY27 (management comfortable with 5.5%-6%), subject to geopolitical impact; management overlay of INR100 crore held.
Cost-to-income ratio guided at 57%-59% for FY27; no FY28 guidance given.
Quarterly run rate of more than 1 million new accounts to be maintained; Q3 opex expected to rise with festive spends.
capex_capacity: No capex plans, capital expenditure figures, or commissioning timelines were discussed on the call; the transcript contains no capacity or utilisation metrics for the business.
Operating cost was INR2,649 crore in Q2 FY27, up 7% YoY and flat QoQ; management attributed the flat run-rate to investment in business growth, with Q3 opex expected to rise on festive spends.

Cost-to-income ratio was 58.7% in Q2 (up 193 bps YoY); guidance for FY27 is 57%-59%. No FY28 cost-to-income guidance was given (management: 'Not as of now' for next year, aiming to reduce it if possible).
demand_pricing: Festive season started around 11 October 2026 versus 22 September 2025 last year, which management cites as the main reason for the weak YoY spend comparison.
EMI offtake is rising as mobile phone prices increase; point-of-sale EMI subvention moved from around 16% to 16.5-17% over recent months, and conversion-to-EMI rates were also raised.
Interchange income rose in Q2 as networks increased rates on certain categories; management says the higher level is sustainable within a range.
Revolver rate at 22% and interest-earning assets stable at 55%; EMI share of book at 33%, revolvers 22% of book, and 45% of portfolio is transactor.
Co-brand additions: Google Pay Flex SBI Card and Advantage SBI Card on YONO; Eternal co-brand card launched; existing co-brands include Tata Neu, PhonePe, Google Pay, Flipkart and BPCL.

qa_highlights.question: Will spends and receivables inflect in Q3, and how long will it take for spend growth to reach double digits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated that receivables growth starts in H2, from Q3. Spend growth is expected in the mid-teens to high-teens for FY27. Early festive EMI conversion trends are described as encouraging, but still early.

qa_highlights.name: How will NIM evolve given higher cost of funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Levers are optimising borrowing mix (working capital loans about 70-80 bps cheaper than CP), raising yields on the EMI book and converting transactors to EMI. Yield hikes are already in place, and management expects NIM to stay stable.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 6% credit cost guidance conservative given 5.5% run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 FY27 credit cost was 6.05%. Management sees 5.5%-6% as a comfortable range and does not expect credit costs to moderate much beyond that. The INR30 crore was a management overlay, not a provision.

qa_highlights.question: Why did corporate spends dip, and does opex stay in line?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate spends were let go for margin reasons. Opex was flat QoQ, but investment in growth was cited, and Q3 opex is expected to rise with festive spends. Cost-to-income guidance of 57%-59% is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the CIF bank share rise to 46%?
qa_highlights.answer: About 10% of the portfolio was reclassified after a granular review of account features and channels. Management said the previous quarter would have shown the same bank versus open-market split on the new basis.

risks_watch: Rate pressure: repo hike already done, with another ~50 bps expected; borrowing mix and EMI repricing must offset cost of funds to hold NIM at 10.8%.
Geopolitical and macro risk (West Asia conflict, energy prices, inflation) could raise credit costs; INR100 crore management overlay is held.
Receivables growth is still unguided; transactor share (45%) can move quickly and affect IEA and yield.
Opex and cost-to-income could drift up from Q3 with festive spending and customer acquisition.
Fee income and the regulatory focus on fee cuts across lenders; management says interchange grows with spends and instance-based fees with CIF.

543187|2026-03.headline: Hitachi Energy India Q4 FY26 revenue rose 46.2% YoY to Rs 2,754.1 Cr, with record order backlog of Rs 29,555 Cr at FY26 end.
543187|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 orders were Rs 2,422.5 Cr (up 10.6% YoY) and revenue was Rs 2,754.1 Cr (up 46.2% YoY), with PAT of Rs 330.5 Cr. For FY26, revenue reached Rs 8,147.7 Cr (up 27.6%) and PAT Rs 987.8 Cr (up 157.3%), while FY26 orders were broadly flat at Rs 18,456.5 Cr (up 1.6%). Management highlighted completion of the 1,000 MW Mumbai City infeed HVDC project and a new Rs 2,000 Cr capex approval, taking cumulative capex to nearly Rs 4,000 Cr. Analyst questions focused on weak non-HVDC domestic orders, export mix, margins, and royalty.

segments.name: HVDC
segments.commentary: HVDC revenue in FY26 was about Rs 1,100 Cr, roughly 15% of Rs 8,000 Cr total revenue, per CEO and CFO; management says it is margin-accretive but not yet substantial. The 1,000 MW Mumbai City infeed (VSC) project was commissioned in FY26.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue was about 25% of FY26 revenue and export orders are in a similar range, though lower in Q4 due to large domestic orders; management cites a 25-30% average, with a 3-pronged model (allocated markets, global feeder factory products like 66 kV breakers and COMBIFLEX relays, and component contract manufacturing).

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: Q4 services orders were high, driven by a control and protection upgrade for MSETCL in India. Management named strengthening India services as a key pillar.

segments.name: Transmission / Transformers
segments.commentary: Transmission order intake showed a small dip in FY26 due to mismatch in large order values versus FY25. Management says the transformer pipeline is very strong and the temporary slowdown is behind them.

segments.name: Data centers, renewables, industry
segments.commentary: Order intake grew across industry, data centers, railways and renewables in FY26. Management says data centers are under 2 GW in India today, with a projected 6-9x expansion; Hitachi targets about 15% of data center capex as addressable.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give forward-looking numbers; CEO said 'we don't give any forward-looking numbers going forward' when asked about FY27 domestic non-HVDC order inflow.
Pipeline described qualitatively as very strong across renewables, data centers, transmission and transformers, excluding HVDC; industries described as intermittent but recovering.

HVDC: management said there is no capacity limitation to take more HVDC projects in the coming year or year after; at least 3, if not 4, HVDC projects expected in the pipeline over the next 2 years, with both LCC and VSC.

New greenfield large power transformer plant at Karjan, Vadodara: groundbreaking on 12 June; capacity baseline 30 GVA, up to 40 GVA depending on product mix; completion targeted by last quarter of CY2028.
Oct 2024 capex programme projects are under way and take 3 to 4 years to complete.

Data centers: India data center capacity under 2 GW, with projections of 13-18 GW; management cited 6-9x expansion. Hitachi treats each data center as 15% of addressable capex; management declined to give an absolute Hitachi figure.
Export share guided as a ballpark of about 25-30% on average, excluding large lump orders such as HVDC; management declined to give exact numbers.
Price pass-through: most of the portfolio has commodity price variation clauses; freight costs linked to Hormuz-related disruption are not passable and are being managed.
Management said the transformer pipeline is very strong and the transmission slowdown is behind them; transformer delivery lead times cited as 12-15 months depending on the product.
capex_capacity: Board approved additional Rs 2,000 Cr capex in Q4 FY26, over and above the Oct 2024 programme; cumulative capex close to Rs 4,000 Cr.

New greenfield large power transformer facility at Karjan, Vadodara, Gujarat, to make LPTs and HVDC converter transformers, targeted for completion by Q4 CY2028; capacity baseline 30 GVA, up to 40 GVA by product mix.
Oct 2024 capex programme projects are under way and take 3-4 years to complete, per management.
Bangalore factory adding 7th and 8th lines for power quality products, on top of 6 existing lines.
Management said the capacity addition is demand-driven and not aimed at local content requirements or product gaps.
demand_pricing: Order backlog Rs 29,555.3 Cr at 31 Mar 2026, up 53.6% YoY; management cited multi-quarter revenue visibility.
Domestic non-HVDC orders: an analyst said they fell in FY26 versus FY25; management said investigation showed no decline and that growth occurred in domestic business.
Price pass-through: most of the portfolio has commodity price variation clauses; freight and Middle East related costs (Hormuz) are not passable and are being managed.
Royalty: management said new technologies and products (e.g., data centers, energy storage) are sourced from the parent and royalty is paid to access them; R&D is managed centrally at the parent.
Local content: management said it exceeds the recent government local content requirements.

qa_highlights.question: How are export orders generated, and do you compete with parent entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a 3-pronged model: allocated markets developed long-term with local sales offices, global feeder factory products (66 kV breakers, COMBIFLEX relays) sold directly or via Hitachi offices, and component manufacturing for other Hitachi factories. Management said no two Hitachi companies compete in the same market.

qa_highlights.question: Why are HVDC margins below peers and what is the HVDC share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: HVDC revenue was about Rs 1,100 Cr, roughly 15% of FY26 revenue of Rs 8,000 Cr; HVDC is margin-accretive but not large yet. Services, exports and base business are the focus.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sequential gross margin decline in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed the sequential contraction to product mix. Gross margin for FY26 improved about 200 bps to 40% from about 38% in FY25.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for non-HVDC domestic orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said non-HVDC domestic orders had not declined on investigation. It noted some capacity is being absorbed by the HVDC portfolio. Management did not give forward numbers and said the pipeline is strong across renewables, data centers and transmission.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new capex capacity and its phasing?
qa_highlights.answer: The new Karjan plant adds 30 GVA baseline (up to 40 GVA). Management called demand multi-year and said the plant completes by Q4 CY2028; groundbreaking is on 12 June.

qa_highlights.question: What is the data center opportunity for Hitachi over five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India data center capacity is under 2 GW versus projections of 13-18 GW. Hitachi targets about 15% of each data center's capex as addressable, and did not give an absolute Hitachi figure.

risks_watch: Gross margin volatility from product mix; Q4 sequential decline cited by an analyst.
Commodity inflation, elevated freight and Middle East-related supply chain pressure, with non-passable freight costs.
Royalty payments to the parent rising as new technology is sourced; other expenses at 16.9% of revenue in FY26.
Non-HVDC domestic order intake: management disputed an analyst's view of a decline, but the FY26 backlog growth is HVDC-led.
Execution on the Karjan plant and the Oct 2024 capex programme (3-4 year timelines).
Unrealised exchange loss of Rs 31.5 Cr in Q4 FY26.

543187|2026-06.headline: Hitachi Energy India Q1 FY27: revenue up 68.6% YoY to INR 2,493.7 crs; orders INR 5,096.5 crs with backlog at INR 32,222.1 crs.
543187|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 68.6% YoY to INR 2,493.7 crs, driven by execution of the existing backlog. Operational EBITDA grew 135.0% YoY to INR 399.9 crs, including a INR 36.37 crs unrealised forex loss, and PBT rose 120.2% YoY. Order intake was INR 5,096.5 crs; excluding the large Q1 FY26 HVDC order, orders grew 26.1% YoY and 39.7% QoQ. Management said gross margin fell YoY on product mix but improved QoQ. The quarter's wins included a first BESS order, a Europe grid-link order and data-centre orders.

financial_highlights.change: +26.1% YoY and +39.7% QoQ excluding HVDC (comparable basis)
+135.0% YoY; includes unrealised forex loss of INR 36.37 crs

segments.name: Product orders
segments.commentary: Management said product orders were the largest contributor in Q1 FY27; the order book is diversified across end-markets and EPC and OEM channels.

segments.name: Utilities and HVDC
segments.commentary: Management named Utilities and HVDC as core businesses. A large HVDC order of about INR 1,700 crs was in the quarter, and the Khavda HVDC project is ramping while Bhadla is starting.

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: Services business unit was described as focused on continuity and resilience of the installed base; no figures given.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the HVDC revenue contribution to build in years two and three, with first-year execution on the lower side.
A greenfield HVDC project is under bidding and is expected to be awarded in about six months.
Railway projects are progressing slower than planned and are expected to pick up in the second half of FY27; transmission weakness is described as timing-related.
Karjan (Vadodara) transformer factory, the company's 20th manufacturing facility, began construction in June 2026 with targeted commissioning in December 2028.
Data-centre visibility is described as strong; management referenced a 15 GW by 2030 opportunity, contingent on government support.
capex_capacity: 20th manufacturing facility at Karjan, Vadodara: construction began June 2026; targeted commissioning December 2028; designed as a fully digital and smart factory.
Capex is aimed at capacity expansion and localising components toward end-to-end manufacturing in India; no capex amount was disclosed.
BESS offering is modular and containerised, excluding batteries; PCS is not yet localised and localisation of BESS is still needed.
Depreciation rose QoQ on ongoing capex for capacity expansion; finance cost broadly stable.
demand_pricing: Order wins included a 2 GW wind evacuation order in Europe (three transmission links delivering 6 GW; value about INR 1,700 crs per management, a combination of three orders with a services focus), a 165 MW / 330 MWh BESS in Andhra Pradesh, and 400 kV GIS/GIB for a 100 GW solar park in western India.
Multiple data-centre orders from hyperscalers, including a 40 x 2,500 kVA project in Hyderabad.
Material costs as a percentage of revenue stayed within the historical range; management said 60-65% of orders are pass-through and there was no material commodity impact this quarter.
Management said the entry of Chinese players in GIS and transformers is not expected to have a material impact, citing existing competition in other forms; no major threat from TBEA.
Gross margin fell YoY on product mix (management did not give quantum) but improved QoQ, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What was the value of the Europe 2 GW order and the export share?
qa_highlights.answer: The Europe order is a combination of three orders valued at about INR 1,700 crs, with services and support focus. Export contribution to revenue is around 25%, which is the current run rate.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin contraction YoY of over 350 bps: what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin improved QoQ and only slightly contracted YoY, mainly due to product mix; the quantum was not given.

qa_highlights.question: BESS offering, competition and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Offering is a modular, scalable, end-to-end solution excluding batteries, with digital layers and battery management integration. Margin profile is hard to state yet as the technology matures and localisation is needed.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 FY27 revenue comes from HVDC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a breakup; said there is some HVDC contribution, with full contribution expected in later years.

qa_highlights.question: Data-centre order size and momentum?
qa_highlights.answer: Multiple data-centre orders rather than one large order; visibility is strong, with long-lead items such as GIS and dry transformers being secured by customers. Management referenced 15 GW by 2030 if government support continues.

qa_highlights.question: Commodity price exposure outside transformers?
qa_highlights.answer: No material impact this quarter; 60-65% of orders are pass-through and small impacts can be managed.

risks_watch: Gross margin trajectory: YoY contraction on product mix, and the margin profile of the new BESS business has not been quantified.
HVDC revenue ramp is back-ended; execution of Khavda and Bhadla is a key monitor.
Competitive intensity from Chinese entrants in GIS and transformers and the 60-65% local content rule; no quantified impact.
Railway order slowdown, expected to recover in H2 FY27, and transmission timing.
Unrealised forex and commodity losses (INR 36.37 crs in Q1).

Evasive on specifics: management declined to give HVDC backlog share, HVDC revenue contribution, BESS margins, segment-wise value of the Kinet Railway opportunity, and the quantum of YoY gross margin change.
key_quotes: We have started the FY27 on a strong note, delivering robust growth in both orders and revenues.

rows.why: A greenfield HVDC project is under bidding and expected to be awarded in about six months, against a backlog of INR 32,222.1 crs.

rows.why: Multiple hyperscaler data-centre orders were won (including 40 x 2,500 kVA in Hyderabad) and management cites 15 GW by 2030 opportunity, contingent on government support.

543212|2026-03.headline: Borosil FY26 revenue rose 8% to INR1,195.9 crore but operating EBITDA was flat at INR176.7 crore as Hydra flask supply disruption from the BIS QCO hit margins.
543212|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations reached INR1,195.9 crore (up 8% from INR1,107.8 crore), while pre-exceptional operating EBITDA was flat at INR176.7 crore and margin fell to 15.1% from 16.3%. Q4 FY26 revenue grew 5.2% to INR284.1 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.5% from 14.2%, with the West Asia LPG supply disruption temporarily shutting the borosilicate and opal glass furnaces. Management attributed the Hydra shortfall to BIS/QCO-related supply chain problems and said the company is adding in-house flask capacity and solar power to offset cost pressures. Net debt at consolidated level was INR49.7 crore at FY26 end.

segments.commentary: Sales INR411.9 crore in FY26 vs INR383.8 crore in FY25, +7.3%. Utilisation is 90-95% and the category has slowed.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR295.5 crore in FY26 vs INR252 crore, +17.3%. Roughly two-thirds is made in-house, the rest is outsourced.

segments.name: Non-glassware (appliances, insulated bottles/flasks, cookware)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR463.7 crore in FY26 vs INR452.9 crore, +2.4%. Hydra flask sales were hit hard by non-availability under the BIS/QCO regime.

guidance_outlook: Management targets revenue growth of 15-20% YoY and EBITDA margin near 20% in the medium term.
Solar 20 MW plant with BESS (INR75 crore capex) to be commissioned in Q1 FY27; expected FY27 EBITDA benefit about INR28 crore, with solar taking care of about 61% of power needs after phase III.

Hydra flask in-house manufacturing (INR65 crore, subsidiary Stylenest India): first 2 lines to start commercial production before end-Q1 FY27, third line by end-Q2 FY27. Gross margin uplift of at least 10% expected, but realised only after 6-12 months of stabilisation.
Opalware: muted growth expected for the next year or so; no major opalware capex, debottlenecking only.

Glassware: Bharuch capacity for bottles, jugs and jars (INR42 crore, via outsourced vendor) expected by end-Q3 FY27. Pressware furnace expansion from 25 to 32 tonnes per day (INR50 crore) likely in FY27 or FY28.
Price hikes of 8-10% taken; management believes they are enough to cover cost inflation, but pass-through lags by 1-2 quarters.
FY27 capex about INR110 crore, plus maintenance capex of INR20-25 crore a year. More non-glassware capex under discussion, not yet Board-approved.
Direct incremental gas cost of about INR30-35 crore per annum due to the West Asia crisis, which management said is changing weekly.
BIS/QCO remediation deadline extended to 1 October 2026; appliance inventory built up to cover it.
capex_capacity: Hydra flask plant (Stylenest India): INR65 crore, 3 double-wall lines; first 2 lines in Q1 FY27, third by end-Q2 FY27.
Solar 20 MW ground-mounted plant with battery storage: INR75 crore, commissioning Q1 FY27.
Pressware furnace expansion 25 to 32 tonnes per day with a third forming line: about INR50 crore, FY27 or FY28 depending on furnace life.
Bharuch glassware (bottles, jugs, jars) via Borosil Scientific: about INR42 crore, by end-Q3 FY27.
Current capacity: opalware furnaces of 84 tonnes per day, borosilicate glassware plant of 25 tonnes per day. Opalware utilisation 90-95%, glassware running close to 90%.
demand_pricing: Hydra flask volumes were hit by product non-availability from the BIS/QCO implementation; management estimated about INR100 crore of Hydra loss in FY26 (per a prior interview), with losses in H1 and more in H2.
Chinese dumping of borosilicate and other glass is pressuring margins. An anti-dumping application covers only borosilicate glass; the decision is expected in 6-9 months.

Gas cost rose sharply from the West Asia crisis. Q4 FY26 furnaces at Jaipur and the borosilicate pressware site were shut for LPG-related supply restrictions; management said the shutdown did not cut sales because of inventory, but it did hit fixed-cost absorption.
Opalware competition: management disputed dealer reports of aggressive pricing and said pressure is on costs, not price.
Advertising and sales promotion rose marginally to about INR88 crore from INR87 crore; power and fuel fell to INR78 crore from INR82.4 crore.
Shared service support income (other operating income) rose to INR26 crore from INR18.4 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margins fall in Q4 despite borosilicate ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Chinese dumping, which Borosil can only partly offset with brand premium, plus higher gas and raw material costs in Q4. A price increase was taken but its impact lags.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA saving from solar?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Anand Sultania estimated about INR28 crore at EBITDA level for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the opalware outlook and capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 90-95%. Growth has slowed, and only debottlenecking is planned. No major opalware capex; focus is on other categories.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the cost inflation is covered by price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price hikes of 8-10% are enough to cover cost inflation, with 1-2 quarters of lag.

qa_highlights.question: What is the incremental gas cost and its impact?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said gas cost rose by about INR30 crore for all three furnaces. Management put the direct impact at INR30-35 crore a year, with indirect effects via packaging, freight and wages.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital and inventory rise, and when will it reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Hydra inventory from last year is largely depleted, but appliance inventory was built for QCO and borosilicate furnace output exceeds sales. Management expects inventory to stop growing this year and reverse next year.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin gain from in-house vacuum bottle manufacturing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects at least 10% gross margin improvement, but only after 6-12 months of stabilisation, so not in the first couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company fund rising debt and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt may rise short term by about INR100 crore, but it expects FY27 capex to be similar to operating cash flow of about INR120 crore, so funding is internal.

risks_watch: Gas and LPG cost volatility from the West Asia crisis: direct cost increase of INR30-35 crore a year, plus indirect effects; Q4 furnace shutdowns.
Chinese dumping in borosilicate and glassware; anti-dumping outcome expected in 6-9 months and not yet certain.
Hydra flask recovery depends on the in-house plant ramp-up; margin benefit is delayed 6-12 months.
QCO/BIS remediation deadline 1 October 2026 for appliances; inventory build-up exposes working capital.
Opalware growth has slowed and management expects muted growth for about a year without new product innovation.
Rising debt (about INR100 crore added in the last two quarters, per an analyst) and ROCE pressure from inventory.
Related-party arrangement with Borosil Scientific (cost plus about 5%); management said it is less than 10% of Borosil sales and consolidation is uneconomic for now.
543212|2026-03.management_tone: Candid and somewhat defensive on the year: management openly attributed the flat EBITDA and Q4 margin fall to Hydra supply problems, China dumping and gas costs, while stressing that these are short-term issues. Confident on long-term targets and new capacity, but evasive on the exact Hydra loss and specific margin guidance for FY27.
key_quotes: Borosil has delivered a reasonable performance in FY26 with revenue from operations reaching INR1,195.9 crores, up from INR1,107.8 crores during the last year.

We are now starting a new facility for vacuum-insulated stainless steel bottles, flasks and containers, and also expansion of our injection molding operations for the plastic lids that go on our lunchboxes.

So we are, as a team, fully committed to enhancing the revenue by 15% to 20% year-on-year, and achieving EBITDA of closer to 20-odd percent in the medium term, and we continue to work on that journey.

We do have reasonable amounts of inventory. So if the market supports we can grow even without having grown the -- without growing the production for at least 1.5 years or 2 because of the inventories that we are carrying today.

543212|2026-06.headline: Borosil Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to INR253.6 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 14.6% from 17.8% on a ~INR10 crore West Asia cost hit.
543212|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 9% YoY to INR253.6 crore, with Glassware up 16.8% and Non-glassware up 4.2%, both stated as volume-led. Operating EBITDA fell to INR35.9 crore from INR40.2 crore as fuel and packaging inflation from the West Asia conflict hit margins; management said price increases of 5-7% were taken but realisations lag into Q2 onwards. PBT dropped to INR17.4 crore from INR23.5 crore (last year included a INR7.2 crore one-time stamp duty reversal), and PAT fell to INR12.8 crore from INR17.4 crore. Management reiterated an FY27 EBITDA margin of about 18% excluding other income, and a steady-state ambition of 18% without the conflict impact.

segments.name: Larah Opalware
segments.commentary: Sales INR83.6 crore, up 9.8% YoY from INR76.2 crore, stated as volume-led with hardly any price contribution. Management guides roughly 9% growth going forward.

segments.name: Glassware (borosilicate microwavables, serveware, tumblers, lunch boxes, storage)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR65.6 crore, up 16.8% YoY from INR56.2 crore; management said growth was entirely volume-led with price pass-through lagging. Utilisation about 90%.

segments.name: Non-glassware (small appliances, bottles and flasks, cookware, kitchen essentials)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR98.1 crore, up 4.2% from INR94.2 crore. Hydra (vacuum flasks) remained hit by BIS compliance requirements, offset by domestic appliances and stainless steel cookware.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 18%, excluding other income; management framed 14-15% historically and ~18% as the steady-state level without West Asia impact.
FY27 capex estimated at about INR125 crore, with an overall range of INR125-150 crore including solar and opal furnace rebuild maintenance capex.
FY27 consolidated depreciation expected at about INR92 crore.
Solar Phase 3 savings estimated at INR27-28 crore at EBITDA level in FY27; management declined to say how much would be retained after pass-through.
Price realisation from the 5-7% increases expected to flow in from Q2 FY27 onwards.
Long-term ROCE aspiration of 20-24% (later referenced as 20-22%) on the business; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Stylenest India (subsidiary) Hydra plant in Rajasthan: 2 double-wall lines commenced commercial production on 30 June 2026; third line expected in Q2 FY27.

Third captive solar plant in Bikaner: 20 MWp with battery energy storage, commissioned in Q1 FY27; solar now meets about 61% of energy requirement. Further 6.5 MWp (Borosil) and 3-4 MWp (Stylenest) solar under evaluation.
Bharuch, Gujarat glassware plant: capex INR42 crore, sanctioned in Q4 FY26 to make jugs, jars and bottles currently sourced (~INR100 crore sales) from BSL Bharuch; commissioning by end Q3 FY27.

Jaipur borosilicate pressware blast furnace expansion from 25 to 32 tons per day plus a third forming line; capex INR50 crore; commissioning by end Q4 FY28. Current furnace utilisation about 90%; furnace rebuild due Jan 2028.
Opalware utilisation described as full; Glassware about 90%.
demand_pricing: Price increases of 5-7% by category taken across multiple categories (management says some above that); execution started mid-May and realisation lags into Q2.
West Asia conflict net impact on Q1 FY27 about INR10 crore (INR12 crore cited in Q&A), with price increases compensating only a couple of crore.

Fuel cost run-rate: Opalware fuel impact about INR6 crore in Q1, expected to fall to about INR1.5 crore a quarter; borosilicate fuel impact about INR2.5 crore a quarter, expected to fall to INR60-70 lakh. Fuel at 5.8% of sales vs 2.9% a year ago.
Chinese dumping in borosilicate glassware persists despite rupee depreciation and higher freight; anti-dumping investigation pending with authorities, timing uncertain and not included in guidance.
Whiteware (Opalware sub-category) about 10% of Opalware sales vs under 5% last year; management said margins are well below the regular range, so it will not push that mix up.

Omnichannel presence across 24,000+ retail outlets, e-commerce, quick commerce and B2B/export; first two exclusive Borosil brand stores opened in Pune and Gurugram, Jaipur next, capex INR40-50 lakh per store, no store-count target.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Glassware's 16.7% growth was price vs volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was entirely volume-led; price pass-through is lagging and was only a couple of crore in Q1 against about INR12 crore West Asia impact. Price hikes range 5-7% by category.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 margin and capex guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: About 18% EBITDA margin for FY27 excluding other income; capex about INR125 crore, with a range up to INR150 crore including solar and furnace maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Has Chinese dumping eased given rupee depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management says dumping continues with no visible difference despite rupee weakness and higher freight. Anti-dumping investigation is ongoing, and no benefit is assumed in guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 growth inflated by channel inventory stocking ahead of price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management rejected that view, saying price impact arrives only in Q2 and there was no forced sale or retailer stocking. Inventory build is typical ahead of Diwali.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence in ~18% margin given historical 14-16%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified that 14-15% is the historical level and ~18% is the steady-state margin without West Asia impact; FY27 target is for 18% on the year, with improvement dependent on price realisation and lower fuel costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to 20-24% ROCE and why is ROCE around 11%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed low ROCE to heavy capex over three to four years, plus inventory built for BIS challenges. It described 20-24% as a medium-term aspiration; it did not provide a bridge or timeline.

543213|2026-03.headline: Rossari Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record Rs 684.9 crore (+18% YoY), but FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 11.9% from 12.7%.
543213|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue and absolute EBITDA, with revenue up 18% YoY to Rs 684.9 crore and EBITDA up 11% to Rs 77.3 crore, though margin slipped to 11.3% from 12%. For FY26, revenue grew 15% (volume-driven) to Rs 2,396.4 crore while EBITDA rose 8% to Rs 286 crore. March saw raw material price increases of 25-30% that compressed gross margin, and management says these are now being passed through from April. Management rephased the Rs 192 crore capex plan across Rossari, Unitop and Tristar, guided FY27 growth of at least 15% and consolidated EBITDA margin of 12-13%, and flagged plans to exit non-core consumer and institutional businesses.

Other income from Mumbai office sale

segments.name: HPPC (Home, Personal Care and Performance Chemicals)

segments.name: Textiles
segments.commentary: Grew 20% in Q4 FY26. Specialty textile margins described as healthy; some resistance to price pass-through in textile industry. Thailand blending unit started end-March 2026.

segments.name: AHN (Animal Health and Nutrition)
segments.commentary: Grew 14% in Q4 FY26. Highest gross margin among segments per management; premix facility commissioned, with revenue ramp expected from Q1 FY27.

segments.commentary: Growth muted with losses moderating in H2 FY26. Management targets breakeven or profitability in FY27 alongside divestment of lower-margin businesses; B2C working capital about 90 days.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports grew 11% YoY in FY26, with expansion into Latin America, Europe, Southeast Asia and Africa.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of at least 15%, similar to FY26, with upside if the global situation improves; includes Thailand (Rs 50-75 crore peak revenue, inside the 15%).
Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 12-13% for FY27, with the same level expected in FY28; pharma and other higher-margin initiatives expected to help from H2 FY27.
FY27 capex of Rs 50-75 crore, including a pharma facility and an aroma chemicals project; the earlier Rs 192 crore plan is being rephased over FY27 and partly FY28.
Expects new Reliance EO capacity to come on stream around Q3 FY27 (December per another remark), supporting ethoxylation availability.
Targets reducing debt over the next 18 months, with a stated aim of becoming debt-free; plans to divest non-core office space and assets, timing not committed.
Expects asset turn of at least 3-4x at peak utilisation, the basis for a peak revenue potential post-capex.
capex_capacity: Total ethoxylation capacity at Dahej raised to 66,000 MTPA after Unitop commissioned additional capacity; partly capitalised in Q3 FY26 and balance in March 2026.
Ethoxylation utilisation at 90-100%, running 24/7 with no downtime outside expansion work.
Unitop 15,000 MT capacity commissioned in Q2 FY26 was about 10-15% utilised in Q3 and is ramping up in Q4 (exact figure not disclosed).

Premix plant for AHN commissioned; revenue expected from Q1 FY27, full-scale capacity enhancement next year.
Thailand blending unit started end-March 2026, focused on textiles with some AHN; not a full-scale plant.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is robust with no demand-side challenge; agro season depends on El Nino, with a good project pipeline.
Raw material prices rose in March (some 25-30%); management says increases have been passed through from April 1, with pass-through easy for most products and resistance in textiles.
Raw material position stable; EO is domestically sourced; phenol sourced from Thailand, Malaysia, India, China and US, and none from the Middle East now.

Competitors named: Kemin, Cargill, Novus, Zoetis (Vetnex), Natural Remedies, Jubilant (AHN); Archroma, Croda, CHT, Pulcra (textiles); BASF, Dow, Lubrizol, Syensqo, Evonik, SABIC, India Glycols (HPPC).
Top 10 customers about 12-13% of revenue; no single customer above 2% of sales. Sales grew at 25% CAGR over six years, with profit CAGR of 18%.

qa_highlights.question: What growth and consolidated EBITDA margin should shareholders expect for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided minimum growth similar to FY26 (about 15%) and EBITDA margin of 12-13%, maintained in FY27, with pharma initiatives adding from H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the capex postponed after being announced a year earlier?
qa_highlights.answer: Ethoxylation capex was delayed as Reliance revised its expansion plans. The April 2025 plan (amines, pilot plants, R&D; about Rs 190 crore) is rephased over FY27 and partly FY28 for cash flow and ROCE reasons; the R&D spend has moved to Navi Mumbai.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a share buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: No plans for a buyback, per Ketan Sablok.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Thailand plant's revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak revenue of Rs 50-75 crore, included within the 15% FY27 growth target; meaningful ramp-up expected from Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the institutional business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects breakeven or profitability in FY27, along with divesting lower-margin businesses; FY27 should be a very good year for the institutional business.

qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Chari said there is nothing of such at all and no plan at this moment.

Non-core asset divestment has no committed value or timeline; management said it could take one to two years.

543213|2026-06.headline: Rossari Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to Rs 697.2 crore, a record, but EBITDA margin slipped to 11.6% from 12.5%.
543213|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached Rs 697.2 crore (up 28% YoY) and EBITDA hit a record Rs 80.6 crore (up 18.7%), though margin fell to 11.6% from 12.5%. Core B2B EBITDA was Rs 85 crore (up 13%, ~14% margin), with the institutional and B2C businesses dragging margins and remaining flat in growth. PAT was Rs 35.1 crore (up 4.5%). Management is pursuing non-core asset monetisation, B2C exits and product-mix changes, and says Rs 11.6% is the margin base; target is ~15% EBITDA margin in about two years. Raw material spikes, phenol losses of about Rs 5 crore and freight volatility weighed on the quarter.

segments.commentary: Grew ~28% YoY; new Fibre Chemicals Division launched during the quarter.

segments.commentary: Grew ~28% YoY; vitamin premix plant now operational; trace minerals and enzyme premixes added. Pharma revenue was above Rs 50 crore last year and is guided to Rs 70-75 crore this year.

segments.commentary: Growth flat YoY; losses moderated. Institutional EBITDA margin cited at 13.6% vs ~16% last year. Debt in this business about Rs 50 crore; exit of consumer/B2C portion planned, institutional cleaning retained.

Management says 11.6% EBITDA margin should be the base level; steady-state EBITDA margin target of at least 15%, expected in about two years.
Pharma revenue potential of Rs 30-50 crore in the second half of FY27 (Q2/Q3 compliance target), per analyst question on the Rs 70-75 crore figure.

Single EO supplier in India, priced on world EO price; limited negotiating power.
Freight rates rose again after brief easing; new orders taken at higher freight.

qa_highlights.answer: Ketan Sablok said 11.6% is close to last quarter and slightly below last year; margins to improve as utilisation rises, low-margin exits and pharma/aroma mix shift. Wait-and-see for at least two quarters due to pricing and RM pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Is 11.6% the base margin and what is steady-state?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 11.6% should be the base level. Base business ex-B2C is 14-15%; target is around 15% steady-state EBITDA margin within two years after B2C recalibration and asset monetisation.

qa_highlights.question: Exit of B2C business: investment, debt and margin effect?
qa_highlights.answer: No separate investment as assets are shared (Silvassa). Debt in institutional/B2C about Rs 50 crore. Exit releases at least 2-3% EBITDA margin. Institutional cleaning retained; only consumer/B2C exits.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing vs volume growth and growth levers without EO availability?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume ~10% YoY, rest from pricing. Growth from new non-EO products (esters, NMMO, NMM, NFM), trace minerals, vitamin and enzyme premixes; pharma to rise to Rs 70-75 crore this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did domestic-focused peers gain while Rossari did not?
qa_highlights.answer: Single-molecule producers benefited; specialty players absorbed raw material hits. Phenol shipment delay from China cost about Rs 5 crore in the prior quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Saudi Arabia project timeline and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Survey and feedstock/land allocation still in progress; nothing finalised. About 1.5 years to first production after announcement; mix of EO and non-EO products.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost rise and average cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher interest because term loans for capex were capitalised earlier and are now expensed as assets commissioned; run-rate to be Rs 9-10 crore per quarter.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on B2C exits, asset monetisation and utilisation; management declined to guide quarterly numbers.
EO supply (single Indian supplier) expected only by about December 2026; EO-linked growth is delayed.
Raw material and freight volatility linked to West Asia/geopolitics; freight rates rose again after easing.
Thailand and Saudi Arabia ramp-up and pre-operative costs weigh on margins.
Pharma compliance timeline (Q2/Q3) gates the Rs 30-50 crore H2 revenue potential.
Interest costs rising as capitalised projects go into P&L; watch whether run-rate falls to Rs 9-10 crore.

543213|2026-09.headline: Rossari Q2 FY27 revenue rose 19% YoY to Rs 697.6 crore, a record, with EBITDA of Rs 87 crore (12.5% margin).
543213|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 set record revenue (Rs 697.6 crore, +19% YoY) and EBITDA (Rs 87 crore, +21% YoY), with growth led by volume and value-added products. Gross margin was 31.6%, up about 200 bps QoQ on product mix, but core B2B EBITDA margin fell to 14.1% from 14.8% YoY on freight and raw material costs. Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin to about 12% and revenue growth to mid-to-high teens, while citing uncertainty from the Middle East situation. Net debt fell to Rs 221 crore and working capital days improved to 86 from 97 at FY26 end.

segments.name: HPPC (Home, Personal Care & Industrial)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 541.9 crore, +18% YoY; H1 Rs 1,095.1 crore, +20% (H1 growth 24% per Sunil Chari). Growth led by personal care, agro surfactants, adjuvants and oil & gas; ethylene oxide constraints limited ethoxylate volumes and sequential revenue was broadly flat.

segments.name: Textile Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 120.8 crore, +26% YoY and about +14% QoQ; H1 Rs 226.9 crore, +24%. Driven by exports to Bangladesh, Southeast Asia, Turkey and Latin America, plus the Thailand facility and the new fibre chemicals division.

segments.name: Animal Health & Nutrition (AHN)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 34.8 crore, +11% YoY; H1 Rs 72.8 crore, +19%. Q2 is seasonally the weakest quarter; management expects Q3 and Q4 to peak.

segments.name: Core B2B (ex institutional and B2C)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 619.9 crore, +21% YoY; EBITDA Rs 87.2 crore, +15% YoY, margin 14.1% vs 14.8% in Q2 FY26 and 13.5% in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Institutional and B2C
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 77.7 crore, +3% YoY; EBITDA +Rs 0.2 crore vs loss of Rs 3.7 crore in Q2 FY26, after portfolio rationalisation. Management targets positive EBITDA in H2 and for full FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 12% plus/minus; management expects margin improvement only from FY28.
FY27 revenue growth guided at mid-teens to high-teens, down from the 12-14% initial view, given demand and logistics uncertainty.
Peak utilisation of the new ethoxylation facility at Dahej expected about 2 years after commissioning, around end-FY28; peak sales target remains 3x capex value.
Working capital days expected to stay in the 87-90 day range by end-March 2027.
Working capital debt expected to be repaid by about mid-2027; all cash flows to go to debt reduction for now.
Exports targeted at 30%+ of revenue by end of this year (Q2 export share 31%, H1 27%).
capex_capacity: Blended capacity utilisation about 60%; new ethoxylation facility (Dahej) at about 30% and ramping; full healthy utilisation expected by next year as Reliance EO capacity arrives.
Reliance ethylene oxide expansion expected in Q1 FY28; no confirmed incremental EO allocation yet, with confirmation hoped for in the next couple of months.
Capital work in progress was Rs 156 crore at 30 September; about Rs 50-75 crore more capex in H2 FY27, with most projects closing by end-2026 and no major capex in India in the following year.
Remaining projects cover pharma excipients, aroma chemicals, hydrogenation and biosurfactant expansion; no volume figures disclosed yet.

Saudi Arabia: Board approved leasing land to wholly owned subsidiary Rossari International Limited Company for a greenfield plant; early site work (fencing, boundary wall) in coming months. Project details, capex and timelines to come after Board approval, likely in 8-12 months.
Thailand blending facility ramping up for Southeast Asia customers; EXCiPACT registration obtained for the Unitop plant.
demand_pricing: Q2 growth was mostly volume-driven; some product prices were cut as raw material prices eased early in the quarter.
Freight costs roughly doubled to tripled versus last year; not all customers absorb the full freight increase. Phenol and other core raw materials are higher YoY.
Export revenue grew about 34% YoY and about 35% QoQ in Q2; export share 31% of revenue; H1 export share 27%.
Pharma exports were about Rs 50 crore last year; qualification takes 6 months to 2 years, and management expects strong growth this year.
Oil and gas focus markets are India, the Middle East, and Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan; US sales go through distributors with no segment data.
Management declined to give a specific H2 revenue outlook, citing the Middle East situation, shipping routes and container and ISO tank availability.

qa_highlights.question: Where is export growth coming from and what is the export outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Export revenue grew about 34% YoY and 35% QoQ, driven by HPPC and textiles in Southeast Asia, Africa and Latin America, with Thailand helping. Target is 30%+ of revenue from exports by end of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity ramp-up and peak revenue at the new Dahej ethoxylation plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak utilisation is expected about 2 years after commissioning, around end-FY28. The 3x capex-to-peak-sales target is unchanged. Utilisation is about 30% today.

qa_highlights.question: Why did core B2B margin fall YoY, and how will it recover above 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight costs (doubled to tripled) and raw material inflation compressed margins. Some pass-through has been achieved, but freight recovery is still a challenge. No specific recovery date was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saudi Arabia project timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The Board approved land leasing in KSA. Feasibility, feedstock and capex work is ongoing, and the next Board approval and detailed timelines are expected in 8-12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will the gross margin benefit from acquisitions such as Unitop and the move to value-added products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Unitop and Tristar had lower gross margins at acquisition, and in-house ethoxylation now requires advance raw material purchases, which lengthened working capital. Gross margin is better than at end-2021 when the three businesses are combined.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the working capital debt and the net debt trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects working capital debt to be repaid by mid-2027. Net debt fell to Rs 221 crore; H1 operating cash flow was about Rs 131 crore.

risks_watch: Ethylene oxide supply from Reliance is a constraint; the expansion is expected in Q1 FY28, but incremental allocation is not yet confirmed.
Freight and logistics costs are high because of Middle East and Red Sea/Hormuz disruptions, and the core B2B margin fell 70 bps YoY to 14.1%.
The FY27 margin guide of about 12% is below H1 levels of about 12%; the company has not given a clear margin path beyond FY27.
Institutional and B2C is only at breakeven, and plans to sell this business remain undetermined in timing and value.
ROCE has fallen to low teens and is expected to recover only from next year; the Saudi capex return profile is not yet disclosed.
AHN growth has slowed; the seasonal peak in Q3 and Q4 must deliver.

543220|2026-03.headline: Max Healthcare Q4 FY26 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR 2,664 crore, but EBITDA margin slipped to 26.8% on chemo-drug discontinuation and higher ALOS.
543220|2026-03.overview: Network gross revenue grew 10% YoY and 2% QoQ to INR 2,664 crore, and operating EBITDA rose 8% YoY to INR 682 crore, marking the 22nd consecutive quarter of YoY growth. Margin fell to 26.8% from 27.2% a year ago, as higher ALOS (up 9% YoY) and the discontinuation of select high-value chemotherapy drugs for institutional patients weighed on ARPOB (INR 77,900) and oncology share. For FY26, revenue grew 16% to INR 10,538 crore, EBITDA rose 14% to INR 2,638 crore and PAT rose 22% to INR 1,631 crore. Management also completed control of Kalinga Hospital (250 beds, Bhubaneswar) and approved a INR 1,400 crore, 700-bed greenfield in Lucknow.

Some of the loss is permanent, with oncology share expected at 21-22%. CGHS reconsideration timing is uncertain.

qa_highlights.answer: Annual chemotherapy billing is down about INR 200 crore gross (about INR 140 crore net of GST). Q4 has the full impact, with discontinuation starting October 2025. CGHS rate revision adds INR 100-110 crore annualised so far, with INR 30-40 crore still to come.

qa_highlights.question: Which hospitals have doctor cost pressure, and will Q4 doctor costs (about INR 435 crore) stay at this level?
qa_highlights.answer: Doctor hiring followed the 25-30% capacity addition in late 2024 and the current 20%+ brownfield rollout across Mohali, Nanavati, Smart and Lucknow. Management expects doctor cost ratios to decline with operating leverage. Kalinga will add manpower but will not move the needle.

qa_highlights.question: How do the Lucknow land bank and the Shaheed Path greenfield fit together, and is there cannibalisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Gomti Nagar (27 acres) will reach 570 beds, with another 200-300 beds planned there. Shaheed Path (5+ acres) is a 700-bed phased project over about 3 years, expandable to about 900 beds. It is a multi-location cluster strategy rather than cannibalisation.

capex_capacity: Brownfield: over the last two quarters, phased commissioning of more than 20% additional brownfield capacity at Mohali, Nanavati (Mumbai) and Max Smart (Delhi); remaining beds to be operationalised over the next 2-3 months. Management also expects another ~10% capacity from the 500-bed Gurugram greenfield on commissioning.

Gurugram Sector 56 (500 beds): interior and facade works started; commissioning targeted by end of FY27 after slipping from earlier 'middle of second half' guidance, due to labour attrition during state elections, LPG shortage affecting contractor labour (company now serving meals to ~1,100-1,200 workers) and about a couple of months of delay. Initial operations expected at ~200 beds; breakeven targeted within FY28 (Dwarka precedent: 300 beds, started with 140, breakeven in 6 months vs 12-month guidance, H1 EBITDA loss ~INR 35 crore).

Max Lucknow Gomti Nagar: 426 beds currently, rising to 570 beds over the next 2 quarters; further 200-300 beds planned on the 27-acre Gomti Nagar land bank over time. Lucknow Shaheed Path: 700-bed greenfield approved at INR 1,400 crore, phased over ~3 years, expandable to ~900 beds; 5+ acres.

Pipeline (commissioning in next 2-3 years): Max Nagpur 100 beds by FY28; Zirakpur, Mohali 400 beds in FY28; Max Dwarka 260 beds (building plan submission underway, 24 months); Max Vaishali 200 beds (awaiting building plan approvals, 24 months post approval); Max Patparganj 400 beds with D-wall construction started, commissioning by FY29. Dwarka brownfield of 200-plus beds being planned; Dwarka oncology centre to start next month.

Kalinga Hospital (Bhubaneswar, 250 beds, 10-acre site): controlling stake acquired in May 2026, consolidation from Q1 FY27; about INR 10 crore annual EBITDA; plans to revamp and expand. Acquisition consideration not discussed.

FY26 capital deployment: INR 1,627 crore into ongoing expansion projects and facility upgrades at newer units, INR 131 crore for land at Vaishali, INR 146 crore dividend paid; Q4 deployment INR 328 crore.
demand_pricing: Network Q4 occupancy above 75% despite higher operational beds; OBDs up 8% YoY and 4% QoQ; ALOS up 9% YoY due to simultaneous multi-location brownfield rollout, expected to tighten over time.

ARPOB INR 77,900 in Q4, after absorbing higher ALOS and discontinuation of select high-value chemotherapy drugs for institutional patients (CGHS). Oncology OBDs down ~5-6% YoY; oncology share of in-patient revenue 21% vs 26% in Q4 FY25 and 24% in Q3 FY26. Management expects oncology share to hover at 21-22%, not return to 25-26%.

Chemo-drug discontinuation: discontinued since October 2025; annual chemotherapy billing down ~INR 200 crore (gross); net of GST ~INR 140 crore. Earlier drugs were billed at MRP with ~15-16% margins; CGHS now requires ~30% discount to MRP. Management says this is industry-wide but Max is most affected given oncology and institutional mix. Q4 carries the full impact.

CGHS rate revision: ~INR 100-110 crore annualised already flowing; balance INR 30-40 crore (super-specialty rates, at two hospitals so far) to flow over the coming months. Management said CGHS is reconsidering the chemo discount but timing is not fixed. ECHS and PSU patients lack dispensary access to drugs such as Keytruda.

Noida ramp-up: occupancy above 64-65% in Q4 with doctors hired; management says it is in line with expectations. Dwarka at 80-85% occupancy. Management cited a hockey-stick occupancy curve: units break even around 50-55% occupancy, and the real value comes from 60-65% to about 80%.

Other metrics: Max@Home revenue INR 73 crore (+30% YoY, 16 service lines, 15 cities); Max Lab revenue INR 52 crore (+14% YoY, 60+ cities, ~6 lakh patients); international patient revenue INR 227 crore (+12% YoY, 9% of hospital revenue); digital revenue INR 838 crore (~31% of revenue). Q4 doctor costs about INR 435 crore; management expects operating leverage from here.
Management stated the company sees 10-12% PAT margin as the industry's steady state. It said doctor compensation increases in micro-markets are transferred to patients over time.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin was 26.8% in Q4 FY26 vs 27.2% a year ago and 26.1% in Q3; management expects operating leverage as balance brownfield beds open over next 2 quarters, and ALOS (+9% YoY) is temporary, but CGHS chemo loss (~INR 140 crore net annual) partly offsets.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Brownfield beds (~20% added) with remaining beds opening in next 2-3 months; Lucknow Gomti Nagar 426 to 570 beds in 2 quarters; Kalinga (250 beds) consolidated from Q1 FY27; Gurugram 500 beds (~200 initially) targeted by end FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Occupied bed days up 8% YoY and 4% QoQ with occupancy above 75%; growth backed by new beds, though oncology OBDs fell 5-6% YoY and oncology share is set at 21-22%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Network occupancy above 75% despite added beds and Board already approved INR 1,400 crore Shaheed Path Lucknow (700 beds); Dwarka brownfield 200+ beds and Vaishali/Dwarka pipeline in planning, so further announcements are probable.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue guidance raise; oncology share guided to 21-22% (not 25-26%) and chemo billing down ~INR 200 crore gross annually, which caps upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gurugram commissioning already slipped from mid-H2 FY27 to end-FY27 (about a couple of months delay), and oncology share has been cut to 21-22%; further slippage risk remains with labour and LPG constraints.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Dwarka oncology centre to start next month and other specialties are expected to fill the oncology vacuum; no specific new molecule or product launch quantified.

rows.label: CGHS rate revision balance INR 30-40 crore
rows.why: About INR 100-110 crore annualised already flowing from CGHS rate revision, with INR 30-40 crore super-specialty balance still to come at two hospitals so far.

rows.label: CGHS reconsidering chemo discount
rows.why: Chemo billing down ~INR 200 crore gross (~INR 140 crore net of GST) since Oct 2025; management says CGHS is reconsidering but timing is uncertain.

rows.label: Gurugram Sector 56 breakeven in FY28
rows.why: Dwarka precedent of 300 beds started with 140 and broke even in 6 months; Gurugram starts ~200 beds, with H1 EBITDA loss expected around INR 35 crore at Dwarka-like scale.

tone.note: Management was confident on the brownfield pipeline, Dwarka/Noida ramp-ups and Lucknow expansion, but defensive on the chemo-drug discontinuation (oncology share now 21-22%) and hedged on Gurugram slippage; analysts probed the oncology share drop, doctor costs and capex sequencing.

543220|2026-06.headline: Max Healthcare Q1 FY27 network revenue rose 16% YoY to INR 2,982 crore, while operating EBITDA margin slipped to 24.8% amid new capacity and oncology drug discontinuation.
543220|2026-06.overview: Network gross revenue grew 16% YoY and 12% QoQ to INR 2,982 crore, with operating EBITDA up 15% YoY to INR 704 crore. Margin was flat YoY at 24.8% but down from 26.8% in the trailing quarter, which management attributed to new brownfield commissioning and the Kalinga (Max Bhubaneswar) acquisition. Net debt rose to INR 2,384 crore from INR 1,908 crore in March 2026, and free cash flow conversion was weak as receivables built up. Management guided that oncology normalises from Q3 FY27 and announced a medical education foray.

Average occupancy above 75% on 13% higher bed capacity YoY
vs INR 345 crore Q1 FY26 and INR 387 crore Q4 FY26

Q1 FY27; Ashutosh noted operating FCF up only 3%

segments.name: Max Bhubaneswar (Kalinga, acquired)
segments.commentary: Post-acquisition contribution in Q1 was INR 19 crore revenue and INR 2 crore EBITDA, at 50% occupancy and ARPOB of INR 35,000. Pre-acquisition FY26 revenue was INR 154 crore.

segments.name: Oncology (in-patient)
segments.commentary: Share of in-patient revenue fell to 22% from 26% in Q1 FY26 after discontinuing select high-value chemotherapy drugs for institutional patients. Excluding oncology, gross revenue grew 20% and ARPOB grew 9% YoY.

guidance_outlook: Oncology expected to start normalising from Q3 FY27 and be fully normalised from Q4 FY27.
Max Smart's remaining 50% of the 400-bed brownfield tower to be handed over in Q1 FY27 (current quarter); Nanavati's remaining 50 beds also to be operational this quarter.
Management expects Smart and Nanavati EBITDA to ramp within 2-3 quarters of operations; Nanavati Phase 1 to achieve corporate-average margins without waiting for Phase 2.
Kalinga turnaround targeted within about 12 months, with occupancy and ARPOB targeted to rise 50-80%, plus 200-250 new beds.

Insurance: 6% automatic price revision expected at September-October 2026 renewals; CGHS super-specialty rates flowing from June, with INR 140 crore annual CGHS benefit tracking as roughly INR 35 crore per quarter from June.
Medical college plan: about INR 300 crore per 150-seat college, funded through internal accruals, with ROCE above 25-30% indicated; commercial operations expected over the next few years.
Net debt expected to rise marginally by year-end given capex; net debt/EBITDA targeted at 2.5x only if acquisitions are made.

Expansion pipeline: Max Lucknow +100 beds (next two quarters); Sector 56 Gurugram 500 beds phased from end-2026; Nagpur 100 beds and Zirakpur 400 beds in FY28; Pitampura 200 beds in FY29; Patparganj 400 beds by end-FY29; Dwarka 260 beds, Nanavati Phase 2 271 beds and Pune 450 beds by FY30.
capex_capacity: Max Vaishali: board approved INR 425 crore capex for a 202-bed brownfield tower, taking the hospital from 387 beds; construction started and commissioning expected before FY30. Management confirmed this is the same tower previously planned for FY29.
Max Smart: 50% of the 400-bed brownfield tower operational; beds opened are at about 80% occupancy with oncology focus.
Nanavati: remaining 50 beds operational this quarter; Phase 1 beds at about 80% occupancy; Phase 2 (271 beds) to take about 2.5 years and requires shutting about 100 beds.
Network free cash flow INR 397 crore; INR 337 crore invested in ongoing capacity projects and INR 386 crore on acquisitions (Kalinga and Yerawada).
Pune greenfield SPV acquired and now a subsidiary; 450-bed Pune project has IOD and is expected by FY30. Thane and Shaheed Path approvals: 30-36 months delivery after about six months of approvals.
demand_pricing: Occupancy stayed above 75% despite 13% YoY bed capacity growth.
Institutional (CGHS/PSU) share of in-patient revenue fell to 22%, and management said the decline will continue on current infrastructure.
Insurance negotiations ongoing with GIPSA and others; management denied any occupancy impact from insurer pressure on admissions.
Management said CGHS institutional business is loss-making on a fully loaded basis but contributes to fixed costs.
DSO rose to 95 days from 87 days, adding about INR 250 crore of receivables versus Q4 last year, mainly CGHS and PSU collections lumpiness; CGHS new portal is now processing bills.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Parliamentary Standing Committee's healthcare recommendation's impact and any reassessment of expansion plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhay Soi said the report is focused on affordability and that the company is not reassessing expansion; he said any viability issue could become a consolidation opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Will Max Smart and Nanavati beds drive EBITDA quickly given 80% occupancy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA should start rising by the second or third quarter of operations as ARPOB improves after occupancy ramps; Nanavati Phase 1 is already in that curve.

qa_highlights.question: What are the medical college economics and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated INR 300 crore for a 150-seat college, targeting ROCE above 25-30%, starting at Lucknow and funded fully from internal accruals. PG courses are also planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FCF grow only 3% when EBITDA grew 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Yogesh Sareen attributed the gap to a receivables build-up (DSO 95 days vs 87), and a higher effective tax rate. FCF conversion was about 56% against the usual 62-65%; he expects normalisation as the new CGHS portal clears bills.

qa_highlights.question: Will oncology and institutional share recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Oncology is expected to normalise from Q3 FY27 and be fully normalised by Q4. Institutional share is expected to keep falling on present infrastructure.

qa_highlights.question: Will opex rise materially before Gurugram comes up?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhay Soi said indirect cost growth came from new capacity at Mohali, Nanavati and Smart plus Bhubaneswar; no major opex increase is expected, so revenue growth should flow to EBITDA.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from new brownfield capacity and Kalinga: EBITDA margin 24.8%, down from 26.8% in Q4 FY26.
Receivables (DSO 95 days) and CGHS collection lumpiness; FCF conversion about 56% vs usual 62-65%.
Kalinga minority shareholder (39% equity, based outside India) litigation over share purchase; company says it has full control.
Net debt up to INR 2,384 crore; management expects it to rise marginally by year-end while capex continues.
Parliamentary Standing Committee's 176th report on affordability and possible FDI caps; no hospital consultations so far.
Insurance renewals in September-October 2026 and whether the 6% automatic price revision holds.
543220|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on capacity ramp-ups, the acquisition playbook and the medical education opportunity. More cautious and deflecting on CGHS economics, receivables and the Kalinga minority shareholder dispute, and it declined to give regional disclosure in the usual form.
key_quotes: We started the financial year with healthy momentum across the Network, recording year-on-year growth of 16% in revenue and 15% in operating EBITDA.
A hospital does not admit a patient, a doctor admits a patient.
We want to avoid giving solo hospital data.
So, one is that oncology will start to normalize from Q3 onwards.

rows.why: EBITDA margin 24.8% vs 26.8% in Q4 FY26; management expects Smart and Nanavati EBITDA to ramp within 2-3 quarters and oncology to normalise from Q3 FY27, and says no major opex rise is expected so revenue growth should flow to EBITDA.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Smart's remaining 50% of the 400-bed tower and Nanavati's remaining 50 beds are operational this quarter, Max Lucknow +100 beds in the next two quarters, and Sector 56 Gurugram 500 beds phase in from end-2026; bed capacity already up 13% YoY.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.why: No revenue or margin upgrade was given; management guided only to ramp timelines and oncology normalisation, with DSO at 95 days and FCF up only 3% against EBITDA up 15%.

rows.why: Oncology drug discontinuation keeps in-patient oncology share at 22% vs 26%, institutional share keeps falling, and DSO rose to 95 days from 87 (about INR 250 crore receivables build), so FCF and margins may lag until normalisation.

rows.why: Medical college plan (INR 300 crore per 150 seats, starting Lucknow with PG courses planned) and Max@Home (INR 78 crore, +32% YoY) and Max Lab (INR 58 crore, +20%) are growing service lines, though no firm launch date was given for the college.

rows.label: Kalinga turnaround to 50-80% higher occupancy and ARPOB
rows.why: Kalinga post-acquisition Q1 revenue INR 19 crore and EBITDA INR 2 crore at 50% occupancy and ARPOB INR 35,000; plan adds 200-250 beds, but a 39% minority shareholder dispute is pending.

rows.label: 6% insurance automatic price revision
rows.why: Management expects a 6% automatic price revision at insurance renewals, though GIPSA negotiations are ongoing and insurer pressure on admissions is a risk.

rows.label: CGHS super-specialty rate uplift
rows.why: Run-rate of INR 140 crore a year, tracking about INR 35 crore per quarter from June, though CGHS is loss-making on a fully loaded basis.

tone.note: Management was confident on bed ramp-ups, the 6% insurance price revision and medical education, but deflected on CGHS economics, the DSO rise to 95 days, and the Kalinga minority dispute; analysts pushed on FCF conversion of about 56% and the margin drop to 24.8%.

543223|2026-03.headline: Max India Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 58% YoY to INR72 crores and quarterly loss narrowed to INR6.8 crores from INR35.5 crores.
543223|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue reached INR213.4 crores, up 30% from INR164 crores, and the EBITDA loss narrowed to INR83 crores from INR99 crores. Q4 revenue was INR72 crores, up 45% QoQ and 58% YoY, with the consolidated loss at INR6.8 crores versus INR27.8 crores in Q3. Management said the Noida Phase 1 partial occupancy certificate unlocks receivables of over INR150 crores and allows re-filing for Phase 2. Care homes and AGEasy both grew sharply, though care home occupancy averaged lower due to new beds added in Q4. Management is still seeking a fundraise, timing dependent on market conditions.
