qa_highlights.question: When will Estate 361 Phase 2 launch, and are residential collections lumpy?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 launch announcement expected within days as 140 of 180 units are sold; collections are lumpy, with booking fee of INR25 lakh, then 10% on application and another 10%, with construction-linked collections over about 3 quarters, lumpy in FY27 and more regular from FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the management fee outlook for E360, E361 and Noida, and the direct cost?
qa_highlights.answer: E360 about INR130 crores and E361 about INR200 crores lifetime management fee; Noida about INR14 crores pending. Variable cost is about 15% of fee; post-completion annuity is about INR10-12 crores per 250-unit community (60% CAM, 40% discretionary).

qa_highlights.question: Will Noida Phase 2 start and how much is pending on Phase 1?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 sales expected during FY27 after re-approval of building plans; about 440,000 sq ft remaining. Phase 1 construction complete, with INR70-75 crores of pending bills to be paid.

qa_highlights.question: Why no entry into Hyderabad and what is the status of partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Residence entry delayed by unlimited FSI which lets developers maximise density; assisted living in Hyderabad is on the list and to be examined later in FY27. boAt watch product has not taken off as expected, but tech solutions are being worked on; IIT partnership on wheelchairs is a major revenue contributor.

qa_highlights.question: Is AGEasy on track for INR500 crores revenue around FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects continued high growth year-on-year, similar to the past two years, without reiterating the INR500 crore target numerically.

qa_highlights.question: When will the company turn EBITDA and PAT positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to show path to profitability for one or two verticals in later FY27; labour code and minimum wage revisions are a watch item.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of new labour codes and staff costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Labour code impact is about INR3-4 crores across entities, mainly gratuity provisioning, recognised in FY27 as the code came in March 2026. Payroll is about INR80-90 crores; management said the reported top line excludes SPV sales.

qa_highlights.question: When is the fundraise and what about the INR32 crore tax demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Fundraise timing depends on market sentiment; cash comfortable for 3-6 months, with an update expected this year. The INR32 crore tax demand on Dehradun is being contested via rectification for unallowed brought-forward losses; if accepted, it reduces to nil.

Two new projects, Bangalore (about 300 units, potential sales value about INR900 crore, in final diligence) and Dehradun (under 150 units, sales value INR850-900 crore), are expected to help meet the 1.5 million sq ft / INR1,800 crore annual sales ambition for the year; definitive documents pending.
Care Home expansion decision timed for October-November 2026, subject to occupancy trends; no new beds added at present.

qa_highlights.question: What should change in cost and top line by Q4 FY27 for the EBITDA breakeven target, and what are the Care Home bed-addition plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give FY27 numbers; breakeven commitment applies to AGEasy, while Care Homes need 8-10 quarters per bed to turn profitable. No new beds are being added now; expansion decision is timed for October-November 2026 subject to occupancy.

qa_highlights.question: Blended ARPOB for Care Homes once occupancy rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said blended ARPOB should be near INR7,500 as recent bed additions were at higher rates.

qa_highlights.answer: No Noida revenue was recognised in June; recognition is tied to possession, expected in Q2. qa_highlights.question: Will AGEasy's INR77 crore to about INR150 crore revenue doubling plan hold given Q1 revenue of INR18-19 crore?

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 AGEasy revenue was seasonal, and what are repeat rate and CAC/LTV indicators?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited festive (Sep-Oct) and winter seasonality plus marketplace year-end deals. Repeat rate is about 10-12% (88,000-90,000 repeat customers); the directional target is 20%+, and ROAS (marketplace near 4, D2C 2.5) is used as the efficiency metric.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive threat from hospital chains, developers and financial players, and what is the moat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued services and IP, not infrastructure, are the moat; hospitals would dilute margins in Care Homes; for AGEasy, moats are senior-specific products (3 patents granted, 3 filed) and brand. AGEasy market potential seen at about INR1,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Which business gives highest ROCE, and expected cash burn for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: AGEasy expected to have the highest ROCE, followed by Care Homes (about 23-24%+). Management declined to give FY27-28 projections; it said the EBITDA loss ratio fell from 95% to 63% and will fall further next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Capital plan and incremental requirement?
qa_highlights.answer: Total capital need unchanged for two years, reduced from about USD25 million to under USD20 million; incremental requirement about USD20 million. Second fund raise deferred using credit lines; INR40 crore second pref tranche received in July 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of DLF's senior living entry?

543227|2026-03.headline: Happiest Minds FY26 revenue rose 12.3% in INR to INR2,315 crore (9.2% constant currency) and FY27 guidance of 12.5% CC growth was reconfirmed.
543227|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue was INR604 crore, up 2.8% QoQ and about 11% YoY, with constant-currency growth of only 0.5% QoQ and 6.4% YoY. Management attributed the soft quarter mainly to right-shifted Arttha licence deals and a pause in a large Hi-Tech customer's new product engagement. Full-year constant-currency growth of 9.2% was below the 10% guidance. Management reconfirmed FY27 CC growth guidance of 12.5%, says it is built on a 15% revenue plan, and guides operating margin up about 100 bps to 17.5-18.5% (explicitly not called guidance).

vs 17.3% in FY25; INR401 crore up 12.3%

FY27 planned headcount of 1,050, with most hiring in the GBS unit and the analytics and AI CoE.
Management will target 90%+ of engineers, testers and service delivery staff trained on and using AI productivity tools by end FY27.
Plans to build a dedicated 1,000-person AI and generative AI team by end FY27.

FY27 guidance is organic only; any acquisition would be on top of it, and no acquisition is in the pipeline.

New partnerships: Anthropic (early partner, formalised Q4) and UnifyApps (360-degree partnership), in addition to existing Microsoft and AWS ties.
demand_pricing: Q4 pipeline grew 27% QoQ (record), a mix of new and existing business.
Repeat business about 92-94% of revenue; billion-dollar clients rose from 82 to 91 and contribute about 58% of revenue.
FY26 added 51 active customers to reach 306.

Named wins include a US insurance and financial services provider (product engineering), a global warehouse automation leader (engineering and security), and a European healthcare software company (hospital management modernisation).

Southeast Asia insurer account at $10 million-plus, grown 40% YoY with two large new programmes.
Preferred partner for 4 private equity firms, a source of pipeline. Two new BUs under large-account leaders; aim to create 1-2 $20 million accounts in FY27.
Management declined to give TCV/ACV, citing no industry-standard formula; says it is working on it.
Pricing shifting toward outcome-based models as AI changes service offerings.

qa_highlights.question: Beyond the Arttha right-shift, what caused softer Q4 growth, notably the sharp QoQ drop in Hi-Tech?
qa_highlights.answer: Management tied the Hi-Tech drop largely to one Canada/China-linked customer pausing a newly built AI-driven cooking-hardware product after completion. Healthcare fell 5% QoQ in Q4 after a pharma licence revenue element completed in Q3; EdTech grew 8.4% QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the GBS segment margin decline QoQ, and which AI platforms have adoption metrics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said GBS is an innovation centre with no separate profitability target; its profit shows up in PDES and IMSS. Relay Build has 40% adoption across internal and customer projects. ELAIRA is an AI companion to ELLIPSE, and SecAIGenie, Eduweave and Insurance-in-a-box are other platforms.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 12.5% FY27 guidance is covered by won deals versus pipeline conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a mix. Plans were built bottom-up by industry groups, IMSS, GBS and CoEs, and stress-tested for H1. The P&L is built on 12.5% against a 15% revenue plan. Repeat business is 92-94%, and multi-year deals give some cushion.

qa_highlights.question: Will sales and AI investments rise in FY27, and what are the margin headwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales cost will rise somewhat as open positions are filled and the hybrid BDM model shifts to client partners. AI investment continues. Management says these are not headwinds per se and that margin is still targeted at 17.5-18.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence in FY27 revenue acceleration, and which verticals will lead?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the pipeline, the 92-94% repeat base, large multi-year deals, PE partnerships, and new large-account BUs under Rohit Mathur (Hi-Tech, industrial, EdTech) and Prathamesh Kulkarni (retail CPG, BFSI, healthcare). It declined to give TCV/ACV for now.

qa_highlights.question: Is any of the 12.5% inorganic, and how is the company different from platform players in AI?
qa_highlights.answer: The 12.5% is entirely organic; acquisitions are integrated and no acquisition is in the pipeline. On differentiation, management cited its separate GBS unit, repeatable solutions, an SDLC CoE for AI productivity tools, and a deliberate delay in building a broad platform until experience was gained.

qa_highlights.question: Succession planning, given promoter holding of about 32%.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said succession planning has been an annual Board-reviewed exercise since 2012, with Hogan assessments added last year, IIM Bangalore and ISB programmes, and some leaders hired externally.

Sales-team transition and GBS profitability reporting are open questions.

543227|2026-06.headline: Happiest Minds Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 14.3% YoY to INR629 crore (6.7% in constant currency); FY27 guidance of 12.5% growth reiterated.

Adjusted PAT was INR80.5 crore (12.3% of total income), up 12.9% QoQ and 14.3% YoY, with adjusted EPS of INR5.34. Commissioned 75 MW of Adani's solar project at Khavda and has about 67.5 MW under execution there, due Q1 FY27. BESS EPC revenue of INR43 crore (reported as Q4 revenue of INR46 crore) came via group company Advait Green Energy.

segments.name: BESS and electrolysers (manufacturing build-out)
segments.commentary: Dholera multi-integrated facility is expected to be operational in Phase 1 by Q4 FY27, with 2.5 GWh BESS and 100 MW electrolyser Phase 1 capacity. Management guided INR100-200 crore BESS manufacturing business in FY27 as the plant starts only around September-October 2026.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of 40%-plus in FY27, described as conservative by management; it said FY26 growth was about 80%.
FY27 order book targeted at INR1,600-1,650 crore by end of FY27 against an order pipeline of about INR2,000 crore.
Segment mix shifting by about 10 percentage points a year; FY27 targeted at roughly 65:35 (PTS:NRE).
Margin improvement of about 1 percentage point expected in FY27; electrolyser margins 5%-10% initially, rising to about 20% in the subsequent year.
FY27 total capex of INR300-350 crore, including about INR137 crore for PTS/IPP and INR75 crore for BESS and electrolyser subsidiaries; FY26 PTS capex about INR100 crore funded internally.
Fuel cell: technology transfer with AVL and TECO for a plant in Ahmedabad; manual plant in about 1.5 years, automatic in 2-3 years; management sees about 500 MW of fuel cell demand within 2-3 years.
capex_capacity: Solar EPC physical capacity is about 100-200 MW a year, per management, with QRs now in place for large tenders.
Dholera facility: Phase 1 expected operational by Q4 FY27, covering 2.5 GWh BESS and 100 MW electrolyser capacity; BESS plant to be 5 GWh over time.
Electrolyser module range: 250 kW, 500 kW, 1 MW, 2.5 MW and 5 MW single-stack, designed for a 100 MW project.
NABL accreditation received for the existing OPGW, ERS and stringing tools manufacturing facility.
Management expects BESS plant utilisation of 80%-85% in about a year and a half from start.
demand_pricing: Order execution timelines are typically 6 to 18 months depending on business type.

Largest-ever stringing tools and capital tools order of INR22 crore in Q4; ERS supply for MNRE of INR70 crore; first Uttarakhand EPC order of INR33 crore; GETCO re-conductoring EPC order of about INR27 crore.
Management said cost inflation in metals, fuel and other inputs compressed industry margins; conductor and transformer contracts have price-escalation clauses, but OPGW contracts do not.
New ALMM rules for solar from June 1: management said bids already factor them in, the split of government versus private order flow is about 50:50 to 60:40, and it expects limited cell-price impact.
Management expects fuel cell demand to start in FY26 but deliveries from FY27-28; applications are data-centre backup, ferries and defence.

qa_highlights.question: Why is guidance of 40% growth conservative given the INR1,300 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was a little conservative: FY26 growth was about 80% and it expects robust growth in FY27. Order pipeline is about INR2,000 crore, with an FY27-end order book target of INR1,600-1,650 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 BESS revenue INR46 crore if BOO projects will sell electricity?
qa_highlights.answer: The BOO projects were awarded to the group company Advait Green Energy and booked as EPC revenue (INR43 crore). Electricity revenue will sit in SPVs and be consolidated after COD, likely from FY end.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 capex and margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed FY27 capex of about INR300-350 crore in total and expects about 1 percentage point of margin improvement in FY27. Electrolyser margins are expected at 5%-10% initially and about 20% in the following year.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company pass on commodity cost inflation to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Conductor and transformer contracts have pass-through clauses; OPGW contracts do not. Management said it has factored these into its bid numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Why were four subsidiaries created, and who holds the other 20% of one of them?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiaries were set up for focused growth, bank facilities and future equity raises, with AGPL for electrolysers and solar EPC, the battery company for BESS and C&I, Akara for carbon and Aura for assets. The 20% holder was not answered on the call and was deferred to email.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company fund capex and what about dilution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said funding will use both equity and debt in a mix based on business composition, and equity dilution would happen only if it benefits shareholders. No quantum was given.

qa_highlights.question: When will the company move to pure-play solar EPC and what is the solar EPC capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to bid on large tenders including module-supply projects and win some orders this year. Physical capacity is about 100-200 MW a year.

risks_watch: Operating cash flow was about INR5.8 crore against PAT of INR58 crore in FY26; management attributed this to working capital build-up from the Q4 revenue surge and gave no timeline for conversion.
Debt-equity rose to 0.46x from 0.23x, and management said further capex will need a mix of equity dilution and debt; no quantum was disclosed.
Margin pressure from metal and fuel cost inflation and from the NRE mix shift; Q4 consolidated EBITDA margin of 12.61% compares with 11.73% for FY26 and 12.87% in FY25.
Electrolyser and fuel cell timelines depend on government policy and market opening; the Dholera facility is due Q4 FY27 and fuel cell deliveries from FY27-28.
Ownership structure of the 80% subsidiary (Advait Carbon) was not clarified on the call.

Some answers were inconsistent: management cited Q4 standalone PAT as rising from INR15 crore to INR10 crore, and the Dholera BESS plant start timeline (Q4 FY27 versus September-October 2026) was not fully reconciled.
543230|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the long-term energy transition story and order book, but evasive on specifics such as subsidiary ownership, funding quantum and fuel cell revenue. Management called its own FY27 growth guidance conservative, while acknowledging margin pressure from input costs.
key_quotes: So this year we could achieve about 80% revenue growth, and we are expecting robust growth for this year.
Physical capacity is close to 100 to 200 megawatt a year.
Our margins with our manufacturing facility being opened up for this year and having the sustained program for putting more manufacturing will keep on improved marginally.
So, cash flow is largely INR5.82 crores, which is you have mentioned correctly.

rows.why: Dholera Phase 1 (2.5 GWh BESS, 100 MW electrolyser) is under construction with INR75 crore capex and management guides operations by Q4 FY27 (start around Sep-Oct 2026 per another remark); solar EPC physical capacity is 100-200 MW a year and 67.5 MW is still under execution at Khavda, due Q1 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book reached INR1,304 crore (+159% YoY) with a target of INR1,600-1,650 crore by end FY27, and FY26 revenue grew 80% to INR714.52 crore; 40%-plus FY27 revenue growth is guided.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex guided at INR300-350 crore (about INR137 crore PTS/IPP and INR75 crore BESS/electrolyser), debt-equity rose to 0.46x from 0.23x, and funding will mix equity dilution and debt with no quantum disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management called 40%-plus FY27 growth conservative after FY26 growth of about 80%, with a record INR1,304 crore order book (+159% YoY) and a INR2,000 crore pipeline against an FY27 order book target of INR1,600-1,650 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Metal and fuel cost inflation is compressing margins, OPGW contracts lack price-escalation clauses, and FY26 operating cash flow of INR5.8 crore against PAT of INR58 crore shows working-capital strain; Dholera timing was also not reconciled.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Electrolyser modules (250 kW to 5 MW) are planned for the 100 MW Dholera project, BESS manufacturing is guided at INR100-200 crore for FY27, and fuel cell deliveries from FY27-28 follow a plant that is about 1.5 years away for manual production.

rows.label: Order book target INR1,600-1,650 crore by end FY27
rows.why: Record INR1,304 crore order book against an INR2,000 crore pipeline; large Q4 orders include INR22 crore stringing tools, INR70 crore ERS for MNRE, and INR33 crore Uttarakhand EPC.

rows.label: Cash conversion of FY26 profits
rows.why: FY26 operating cash flow was about INR5.8 crore against PAT of INR58 crore, and management gave no timeline for conversion.

rows.label: New ALMM rules for solar from June 1
rows.why: Management says bids already factor in the rules, government versus private order flow is 50:50 to 60:40, and cell-price impact is expected to be limited.

tone.note: Management was confident on the order book, 40%-plus FY27 growth and the energy transition story, but evasive on subsidiary ownership (the 20% holder was deferred to email), funding quantum and fuel cell revenue; analysts pushed on BOO revenue treatment, capex funding and dilution.

543232|2026-03.headline: CAMS Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record with non-MF revenue up ~24.5% YoY and EBITDA margin back at ~46.5%, while MF revenue was flat (+0.5% QoQ).
543232|2026-03.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue and absolute EBITDA of about INR183 crores, with margin recovering to about 46.5% from 45% a year earlier. Non-MF revenue grew about 24.5% YoY and now contributes about 15.3% of enterprise revenue, with non-MF EBITDA margin above 16%. MF revenue was nearly flat, with AUM at INR55.1 lakh crores (down from INR58.5 lakh crores at one point in Q4 on Middle East-related market weakness) but up 21% YoY. Management guided to sub-5% employee cost growth and sub-9% total expense growth in FY27, flat KRA revenue, and at least 20% non-MF growth.

financial_highlights.value: ~24.5% of growth YoY; 15.3% share of enterprise revenue

financial_highlights.change: Up from ~INR177 crores QoQ; ~INR173-174 crores peak in prior-year Q4

financial_highlights.value: ~9% YoY incl. depreciation; ~7.8% excl. depreciation; <1.5% QoQ
INR 4 per share (subject to shareholder approval); total FY26 payout ~INR305 crores
Just over INR1 lakh crore; CAMS share 76% (from 71% in prior quarter)
Almost INR59,000 crore in quarter; crossed INR20,000 crore in March
financial_highlights.change: +17% YoY vs industry +4%; collection share 57% to 64%

financial_highlights.value: AUM above INR3 lakh crore; 50% outsourced share
Revenue +28% YoY for quarter; KRA non-MF share ~30%

segments.name: Mutual fund (RTA/core)
segments.commentary: Revenue almost flat (~+0.5% YoY); AUM INR55.1 lakh crore, up 21% YoY with 68% overall share; yields stable, QoQ compression under 1% attributed to passive mix shift. Headcount in core MF operations reduced by ~70 YoY.

segments.name: Non-MF (overall)
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~24.5% YoY, broad-based across CAMSPay, AIF, KRA; FY26 non-MF growth ~18% due to weak Q1. Non-MF EBITDA margin upwards of 16%, targeting 20% by end FY27.

segments.name: CAMSPay (payments)
segments.commentary: Payment aggregator (PA) and payment gateway (PG) both grew ~23% YoY; cards business ~25% of quarterly revenue, all non-MF; non-MF now above 50% of CAMSPay revenue.

segments.name: KRA
segments.commentary: Revenue +28% YoY despite demat/broking slowdown; NSE KRA integration added ~13-14 lakh PANs. Industry-wide ~20% fee cut from 1 April 2026 expected to reduce revenue by INR8 crore, offset by INR3 crore NSE KRA uplift; management guides flat FY27 revenue.

segments.name: Alternatives (AIF)
segments.commentary: Revenue +25% YoY; AUM crossed INR3 lakh crore; 44 new full-service mandates incl. 14 new logos; 50% share of outsourced market.

segments.name: Repository / Insurance and others
segments.commentary: Rep revenue +6% YoY. Bima Central active users doubled; LIC started demat-format policy issuance. IR market share expanded to 40%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 employee cost growth guided below 5%; total expense growth guided below 9%, with a stated aim to be lower; increments effective from Q2 FY27.

Management aims to retain Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin (~46.5%) through FY27 after absorbing salary increases, investments and yield compression; no formal margin range given (bad quarter below 45%, good quarter ~46-47%).
Non-MF revenue growth of at least 20% in FY27 (~INR45-50 crore incremental on a ~INR250 crore base), with payments ~INR20 crore, AIF ~INR7-8 crore, Rep ~INR7-8 crore, AA/TSP/pension ~INR15 crore.
KRA revenue guided flat in FY27 after ~INR8 crore price-cut impact offset by ~INR3 crore NSE KRA uplift and new-logo growth.
MF yield decline expected to be less than 3% (historical 3-3.5%); target 20% non-MF EBITDA margin by end of next year.
Revenue expected to grow on flat-to-falling headcount in FY27; ReArch expected to be a 5-year program, about 2 years done, ~3-4% behind schedule curve.
capex_capacity: ReArch cloud-native platform: 9 significant modules; transaction origination module fully built and launching to several thousand integrators; data lake (on Google Cloud BigQuery) to go live in 1H FY27; data warehouse and next-gen transaction origination platform ready within 3-4 months.
Team of close to 200 engineers on ReArch; headcount at FY26 end 8,420 vs 8,324 at FY25 end (ReArch hires >100; core MF headcount reduced ~70).
Form data extraction now runs in production with maker step removed (AI performs data entry; physical checker retained), ~1 million physical forms per month.
SIFs: 6 live as of Q4 FY26 after 4 launches in the quarter; ~8 more licensed or announced, with launches expected May-August 2026.

ConsenPro (DPDP compliance product, built in Think360) launched commercially; ~40,000-50,000 Indian companies expected to need it over 1.5 years. Unified device product (payments and KYC) noted as an adjacency.
demand_pricing: Industry-wide KRA fee cut of ~20% effective 1 April 2026, voluntary and coordinated; KRA base ~INR42-43 crore for FY27.
MF yield compression QoQ under 1%, attributed to passives mix (passives under 10% of AUM); management says no yield cut in individual asset classes. Equity share of AUM ~54-55%.
Mid-sized AMC contract renewals due during FY27; management does not expect material yield decline; a possible 3-5 bps AMC-level pass-through discussed but no concrete RTA fee change agreed.
Licensed domestic AMCs at 31; new AMCs (e.g., Neo, Oaklane) onboarded on scale-play logic. Management says it is selling value rather than price.
IR market share 40%; KRA now number 2 in KRA market after gaining share over ~1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Opex growth of ~10% in FY26 is the lowest in 5 years: how much is deliberate discretionary cost management versus sustainable savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Ram Charan said the cost actions are structural and automation-led, not a one-off squeeze. Headcount rose ~100-120 people YoY, with ReArch hiring offset by a ~70 reduction in core MF operations. Total cost growth was 9% including depreciation and 7.8% excluding it, with QoQ cost growth under 1.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Passive mix shift typically hurts RTA yields more than AMC yields. Is there scope to renegotiate RTA pricing on passives or to gain bargaining power on the active book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said passives are under 10% of AUM and already priced at very low levels, so there is no room to renegotiate. Yield compression QoQ (<1%) came from mix, not from lower rates in any asset class. Ram Charan said the mix shift is an argument to raise with AMCs, but it is not a decisive one.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 3-5 bps AMC fee cut be passed to RTA fees? Is any RTA fee negotiation under way?
qa_highlights.answer: No concrete RTA fee change has been agreed. Discussions may happen, but management said it is comfortable with the price-value equation and does not expect a material impact.

qa_highlights.question: Should yield decline be modelled at the historical 3-3.5% for FY27 and FY28, given that margins have previously dropped from 46-47% to 42-44%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 3-3.5% is the 5-year average and should be used as a conservative model input, with the aim being a lower number, possibly under 3%. On margins, Anuj Kumar said 46% was reached about 5 quarters ago, dropped to 42%, and has now been regained over 4 quarters. He attributed the earlier fall to investments in non-revenue businesses made over 2022-2025.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 guidance for employee cost, overall expenses and EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost growth is guided below 5% and total expense growth below 9%, with increments effective from Q2 FY27. No formal margin guidance was given; the aim is to retain the Q4 FY26 margin of ~46.5% after salary increases, investments and yield compression.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ~20% non-MF growth be built in FY27 with KRA flat, and what is the breakdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a base of ~INR60-62 crore quarterly non-MF revenue, or ~INR250 crore annualised. It needs ~INR45-50 crore of increment: payments ~INR20 crore, AIF ~INR7-8 crore, Rep ~INR7-8 crore, AA/TSP/pension ~INR15 crore (quoted as INR4-5 crore in one place and ~INR15 crore in another), with ConsenPro and GIFT City adding a few crore.

qa_highlights.question: KRA: what is the price cut, and how is FY27 revenue flat after it?
qa_highlights.answer: The industry-wide ~20% fee cut from 1 April 2026 is expected to reduce KRA revenue by ~INR8 crore on a base of ~INR42-43 crore. NSE KRA integration adds ~INR3 crore, leaving a ~INR5 crore gap that management expects to close through new-logo growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is ConsenPro and what is the market opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: ConsenPro is a commercial DPDP-compliance product built inside Think360 from an internal captive offering. It covers consent management, data discovery, regulatory reporting and consulting. Management expects ~40,000-50,000 Indian companies to need it over ~1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Could a single KYC regime through CKYC reduce KRA pricing or volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CKYC is not yet eligible to substitute for KRA KYC. KRA runs a second verification layer (name match, face match, DOB and address against DigiLocker or UIDAI), so the risk is seen as a watch item rather than an immediate threat.

risks_watch: MF yield: the passive mix shift continues to pull yields down. Any AMC pass-through of 3-5 bps could lead to RTA fee discussions. Management guides yield decline below 3%, against a 3-3.5% historical average, and says no concrete RTA fee change has been agreed.

KRA: a ~INR8 crore fee cut from 1 April 2026 is only partly offset by ~INR3 crore from NSE KRA. FY27 flat guidance depends on new-logo growth to fill a ~INR5 crore gap. A possible single-KYC/CKYC shift is a watch item.

Margin sustainability: management is targeting retention of the ~46.5% Q4 margin through FY27 after salary increases, investments and yield compression. Past cycles show margins falling back to 42-44% after investment phases.

MF AUM and asset growth: AUM fell from INR58.5 lakh crore at a point in Q4 to INR55.1 lakh crore, reflecting Middle East-related market weakness. Management says asset growth is awaited after the last two months, and FY27 MF revenue is not guided.

ReArch execution: a 5-year programme with ~2 years done and ~3-4% behind the schedule curve. The data lake is due in 1H FY27, and the data warehouse and next-gen transaction origination platform are due within 3-4 months. Non-MF margin target is 20% by end FY27.

Non-MF growth dependence: ~20% FY27 growth needs ~INR45-50 crore of incremental revenue. The breakdown includes ~INR20 crore from payments, with a new-logo pipeline (SIFs, ConsenPro, GIFT City) still early.
key_quotes: We posted our highest ever quarterly revenue in Q4 '26.
And I expect that this is kind of a baseline number, which will stick.
We will continue to take these cost actions.
So there is not a onetime squeeze that we have done of everything, and it is not going to be repeatable.
We are taking the maker out completely.
We have a team of close to 200 engineers working on this.

Cautious and deliberately non-committal on FY27 specifics: no formal margin range, no MF growth guidance, and repeated hedging on yields and AMC fee discussions.

rows.label: Sub-5% employee cost growth and sub-9% total expense growth in FY27
rows.why: FY26 total cost growth was ~9% incl. depreciation and 7.8% excl., with core MF headcount cut ~70 YoY, and management guides employee cost growth below 5% with increments from Q2 FY27.

rows.label: Non-MF revenue at least 20% growth in FY27
rows.why: Non-MF revenue grew ~24.5% YoY in Q4 and the bridge needs ~INR45-50 crore on a ~INR250 crore base, with payments contributing ~INR20 crore, though the SIF and ConsenPro pipeline is still early.

rows.label: Possible RTA fee renegotiation after AMC 3-5 bps pass-through
rows.when: during FY27 as mid-sized AMC renewals come up
rows.why: A 3-5 bps AMC-level pass-through is under discussion and renewals are due in FY27, but no concrete RTA fee change has been agreed and management does not expect a material impact.

543232|2026-06.headline: CAMS Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose 18% YoY to a record INR183 crore, with margin up 270bps to 46.4% despite muted MF AUM growth.
543232|2026-06.overview: Operating revenue grew 11.5% YoY to INR395 crore and EBITDA grew over 18% to INR183 crore, the highest ever, with PAT up 17%. MF revenue grew under 10% while non-MF revenue grew over 28%, led by Pay (up ~67-70%) and AIF (up ~25%), while KRA declined after the April 2026 pricing reset. Management said July AUM recovered strongly and expects FY27 blended revenue growth of about 13% and EBITDA growth of about 16%. Non-MF margin fell to about 13% in Q1 from over 17% last quarter, which management attributed mainly to the KRA dip.

financial_highlights.change: just under +15% YoY; market share about 67.2%

segments.name: Mutual fund (asset-based)
segments.commentary: MF revenue grew about 11% on asset-based revenue, with absolute MF revenue up under 10%; management sees no quarter-on-quarter yield decline. Equity AUM grew 17.6% and equity net sales and live SIP counts grew ahead of industry.

segments.name: Pay (payments)
segments.commentary: Grew just short of 70% YoY, driven mainly by credit card transactions after the PA licence; management said cards will be grown step by step given low margins.

segments.name: AIF / Alternatives
segments.commentary: AUM crossed INR3.2 lakh crore, grew mid-20s (about 25%), with 50 new mandates won in the quarter.

segments.name: KRA
segments.commentary: Revenue fell YoY after the April 2026 pricing reset (rates down about 29-30%); management expects recovery from Q2.

segments.name: SIF and GIFT City
segments.commentary: SIF: 11 unique SIFs launched, about INR12,000 crore accumulated and about INR1,000 crore net sales per month, nearly 50,000 investors. GIFT City retail: about INR750 crore AUM from first 10,000 investors.

segments.name: CAMS Repository, AA, pension
segments.commentary: Not yet EBITDA positive; management expects CAMSRep to turn EBITDA positive on a Q4 basis. Think Analytics is near breakeven.

guidance_outlook: FY27 blended non-MF revenue growth of about 20%, possibly 22-23%; MF revenue growth of at least 12%; blended revenue growth about 13% and EBITDA growth about 16%.
Non-MF margin expected to recover to about 17% for the year, 'close to 20%' by year-end, per management's varying comments.
Employee cost growth target about 5% YoY for FY27; total cost growth target below 10% per year for the next two to three years.
Enterprise headcount to fall about 5% in FY27; net employee cost benefit expected to be about 3-3.5% rather than 5%.
Operating margin expansion of about 1% a year, with possibility of 1.5%.
PAT margin expected to stay at about 30-31%; FY27 PAT growth about 31% if EBITDA growth is about 45%, per Ram Charan's answer.

On-prem capex about INR75 crore in the coming year, declining later; re-architecture total cost about INR500 crore, of which about INR290 crore capex, with about INR40 crore capitalised in Q1 and at least another INR80 crore in the rest of FY27.
Depreciation expected to rise, not fall, for the rest of FY27 by INR4-5 crore, due to re-architecture capitalisation.
capex_capacity: On-prem capex about INR75 crore in the coming year, falling in later years as cloud migration progresses.
Re-architecture project cost about INR500 crore, of which INR123 crore spent so far; about INR290 crore to be capex on a 10-year amortisation.
About INR40 crore re-architecture capitalised in Q1 FY27; at least INR80 crore more expected in the rest of FY27.
Transaction acceptance module of new platform going live Aug-Sep; full transaction acceptance concept by year-end. Four of eight transaction types live; all expected by November.
About 10% of gross payload converted to AI-based acceptance at maker level, to scale to 100% in 12 months.
demand_pricing: Market conditions muted in April-June; July materially better, AUM close to INR60 lakh crore but not yet there.
SIP collections held at just under INR60,000 crore in Q1; SIP collections and unique investor base grew faster than industry.

Yields: no quarter-on-quarter decline in Q1; compression from 4Q FY26 and 1Q FY26 is now in the base; residual compression for the next 3-4 quarters expected to be small. Historical 2.5-3% annual yield decline cited as likely.
KRA: pricing reset from 1 April 2026 cut rates about 29-30%; some fetch services that were free are now priced. Management says pricing is uniform across KRAs.
Mid-size AMC renewals: a couple concluded and two in discussion; impact on pricing expected to be very muted and already in Q1 pricing.
Non-asset MF revenue down YoY on lower NFO activity, the NSE arrangement winding down and application fees; QoQ also hit by MF Central and OPE.

qa_highlights.question: Expected AUM growth and yield compression behind the 13% blended revenue guidance, and downside risk (line dropped, not answered in full)
qa_highlights.answer: Question was cut off by a line drop before management responded; the outlook was not restated in that exchange.

qa_highlights.question: How many mid-size AMCs are up for renewal this year and is their pricing impact already in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: A couple of mid-size AMC renewals concluded and two more are in discussion; the impact is expected to be very muted and is already in Q1 pricing.

543238|2026-09.headline: UTI AMC Q2 FY27 standalone core PAT rose 31% YoY to Rs 136 crore, while reported PAT fell 14% YoY to Rs 143 crore.
543238|2026-09.overview: UTI AMC reported Q2 FY27 standalone core income of Rs 324 crore (+2% YoY, +5% QoQ) and core PAT of Rs 136 crore (+31% YoY). Consolidated core income was Rs 398 crore and consolidated core PAT Rs 131 crore. Average mutual fund AUM rose to Rs 4.02 lakh crore from Rs 3.93 lakh crore in Q1, with net sales of about Rs 5,720 crore, but equity and hybrid outflows increased, with Flexi-Cap a key drag. Management said several funds were improving on performance, and that SIP AUM was flat QoQ at Rs 45,572 crore. The CEO did not attend the call due to a family emergency.

segments.commentary: AUM about Rs 4.32 lakh crore at 30 Sept 2026, up about 10.97% YoY from Rs 3.89 lakh crore; 24.01% share of NPS industry AUM. 169 new corporates onboarded Apr-Oct 2026.

segments.name: UTI International
segments.commentary: AUM US$1.67 billion (about Rs 16,063 crore) at 30 Sept 2026; clients in more than 30 countries. Revenue flat QoQ; two new fund launches planned by end Q3 or Q4 FY27.

segments.name: UTI Alternatives
segments.commentary: AUM about Rs 4,045 crore, up 52% from Rs 2,669 crore a year earlier. SDOF IV crossed Rs 1,000 crore (Rs 1,131 crore) against a Rs 1,500 crore target plus Rs 500 crore greenshoe.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net outflows rise to about Rs 800 crore in equity and Rs 300 crore in hybrid, and will employee numbers keep falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Flexi-Cap saw large outflows despite some inflows; the fund is now in the first quartile on three-month performance. Two blend-strategy funds are in the top two quartiles. Management guided standalone employee cost at about Rs 95 crore and consolidated at about Rs 130 crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is UTI gaining share in new SIP registrations, and how are ticket sizes trending?
qa_highlights.answer: New SIP registration share is close to 4%, with many SIPs staying. Average ticket size is about Rs 3,100, up over time.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q2 AUM growth came from net inflows versus market appreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Average AUM rose by about Rs 10,000 crore, of which about Rs 5,720 crore came from net sales.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise yields and reasons for the sequential yield movement?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity and hybrid about 73-74 bps, ETF/index about 8 bps, cash/arbitrage 11 bps, fixed income 20-21 bps. Weighted average flat at about 31 bps; marginal change from repricing commissions after the SEBI TER-to-BER change, passed on to intermediaries.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for UTI International and the SIF strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Two new UTI International fund launches planned by end Q3 or Q4. First SIF launch is the Hybrid Long-Short fund in Q3; product choices will follow demand over one to two years.

543245|2026-03.headline: Gland Pharma Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22% to INR17,428 million with a 30% adjusted EBITDA margin; FY27 guided to 12–13% constant-currency growth.
543245|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered record quarterly revenue and EBITDA, led by Dalbavancin launch, tender wins, and new CDMO products, with Cenexi back to positive EBITDA (EUR1 million in Q4). Full-year revenue grew 14.5% to INR64,307 million, adjusted EBITDA margin rose 360 bps to 26%, and adjusted PAT margin reached 16%. Base business (ex-Cenexi) EBITDA margin was 41% in Q4 and 38% for FY26. Management guided FY27 consolidated growth of 12–13% at constant currency, excluding any GLP-1 upside, and a 15% CAGR over the next four years.

segments.name: United States
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR9,716 million (+26% YoY); FY26 INR33,181 million (+11%). 31 products launched in FY26, including 5 in Q4; 24 ANDAs filed and 28 approvals received.

segments.name: Europe and other regulated markets
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR794 million; FY26 INR3,249 million (+11%), supported by the integrated business development model.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,468 million (+17%); FY26 INR6,511 million (+7%). Management said Saudi Arabia shipments were paused, hurting Q4 ROW sequentially; ROW is 2–3% of sales.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR670 million; FY26 INR2,672 million.

segments.name: Cenexi
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue EUR45 million (+4% YoY); FY26 revenue EUR182 million (+11%), with EBITDA improved by EUR16 million. Profitable in Q3 and Q4 FY26; Q4 EBITDA EUR1 million. Target of mid-to-high single-digit EBITDA margin by end-FY27 and mid-teen EBITDA medium term.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: 46% of group revenue and +28% growth in FY26 (Cenexi is 100% CDMO). Base business CDMO is 23% of base revenue, growing 33%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 12–13% on a constant-currency basis, excluding GLP-1 and FX upside; management cited about USD40–50 million of incremental CDMO growth and about INR650 crore from base business plus about INR150 crore from Cenexi.
Cenexi FY27 revenue target of close to EUR200 million, with most growth expected in FY28; EBITDA target of at least mid-to-high single digit by end of FY27.
Base business EBITDA margin guided at 33–35% for FY27; consolidated EBITDA margin around 25–26%.
Consolidated revenue CAGR of about 15% over the next four years; FY28 guided at around 15%, with a step-up in FY29 (about 19–20%+) as complex products launch.
GLP-1 volumes and approvals excluded from guidance; treated as upside. Partner approvals expected in FY27, with some launches from Q3 FY27.
Tax rate expected to decline as Cenexi profitability improves (FY26 ETR about 29%).
capex_capacity: Capex plan of about INR2,000 crore over the next 3 years on top of about INR300 crore in FY26; about INR500 crore expected in FY27. Investments cover ophthalmic suspension line, blow-fill-seal technology (next year), and CDMO dedicated lines.
GLP-1 cartridge capacity at 140 million units; insulin vial and cartridge fills may occupy 30–40 million units over the next couple of years until GLP-1 ramp-up around 2030.
Two new lines commissioned in Q4 FY26 at the Indian base business, one more to go live next quarter.
Cenexi Fontenay ampoule line adds 30 million ampoule capacity by 2027; replacement line to be put in place this summer (August).
Cenexi utilisation: Fontenay near 100%, Osny solid orals about 90%, two other sites at 50–60%.
Acquired a solar plant in India to reduce power costs.
demand_pricing: Dalbavancin launched in the US and Europe in Feb–Mar 2026 with strong demand; Vizient contract won, and management said there was no channel stuffing in Q4.
Multivitamin (MVI) approval received in April 2026, launch expected in the current quarter, with steady revenue contribution.
Three to four recently launched products plus a GPO contract were said to contribute about USD40 million in FY27.
Increased demand for existing products from competitively priced contract wins, aided by procurement cost programs and economies of scale.
Cenexi: 5–6 products signed with Cenexi's own clientele; 3 MAs signed for Cenexi to act as a releasing entity in Europe.
Cenexi won a large hormonal drug contract in prefilled syringes with a European laboratory.
GLP-1: 8 contracts signed, 6–7 more expected soon; CDMO for liraglutide, semaglutide and tirzepatide; no specific volumes or approvals disclosed.

Raw-material and packaging: solvent delays reported; glass and vial suppliers seeking 5–6% price increases, with a possible 1–2% overall margin impact; logistics cost impact on revenue of 1–2%, shared with partners.

qa_highlights.question: Is Cenexi EBITDA-neutral in FY27 at EUR45 million quarterly revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets at least mid-to-high single-digit EBITDA for Cenexi by end-FY27, driven by efficiencies and higher-value product mix rather than revenue scale.

qa_highlights.question: Can Cenexi revenue exceed EUR200 million in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said close to EUR200 million is the FY27 target, with most growth in FY28 when the new ampoule line is commercialised.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 12–13% guidance conservative given FX tailwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is on constant currency; any FX movement is treated as upside. Q4 constant-currency growth and US growth were not disclosed and will be followed up separately.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 140 million unit GLP-1 capacity is contracted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify contracted capacity, which depends on partner projections; announcements would follow partner approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Why was capacity expanded for GLP-1 before demand is clear?
qa_highlights.answer: The new line is a combo vial and cartridge line, with insulin contracts filling it until GLP-1 ramp-up around 2030 (insulin may use 30–40 million units).

qa_highlights.question: Why did Gland acquire Cenexi, and what is its utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Rationale includes European CDMO entry, MA releasing entity, hormone and controlled-substance capabilities; Fontenay near 100%, Osny about 90%, two sites at 50–60%.

risks_watch: GLP-1 timing: no approvals, volumes or contracted capacity disclosed; partner approvals expected in FY27 and launches from Q3 FY27 or later.
Rest of World (Saudi Arabia) shipments paused in Q4, with a recovery hoped for next quarter.
Input cost pressure: glass and vial price increases of 5–6%, possible 1–2% margin impact; solvent delays; logistics impact of 1–2% of revenue.
Q4 one-off milestone and profit-share income (9% and 6% of revenue, as per the management reply) may affect the margin quality.
Leadership: CEO search is active, with a preference for candidates with CDMO and biologics background.
Currency: Q4 constant-currency growth not disclosed; FX gains contributed to other income of INR1,115 million in Q4.

543245|2026-06.headline: Gland Pharma Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR18,003 million, adjusted EBITDA margin 28%, PAT up 47% to INR3,170 million.
543245|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 20% YoY to INR18,003 million, with CDMO and B2B each about 50% of sales and U.S. revenue up 32%. Adjusted EBITDA (after adding back ESOP) was INR5,102 million at 28% margin, up from 25%, while reported EBITDA was INR4,930 million after a INR36 million forex loss. PAT rose 47% YoY to INR3,170 million but fell versus Q4 FY26, which had a INR508 million forex gain. Management announced a 55-SKU, USD90-100 million potential CDMO supply deal, a China-sourced liposomal in-licence, and a INR2,000 crore capex programme now being executed; Saudi Arabia NUPCO tender delays hit rest-of-world sales.

Over the next 4 years, management is working toward roughly 20% growth; a fuller update is planned for the next quarter or by Aug-Oct 2026.

Cenexi FY27 guidance maintained at about EUR200 million revenue with high single-digit EBITDA margin; management expects Q2 to be better than last year.

qa_highlights.question: Details on the 55-SKU strategic manufacturing deal, and how fast will revenue ramp to USD90-100 million?
qa_highlights.answer: Partner is a global specialty pharma company; about 30-40% of revenue is specialty. Products are made in Indian sites; split is about 60% U.S., 30-35% Europe, 15-20% ROW. Tech transfer starts September 2026, first products in 24 months, ramp from 2029 to 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Revised capex estimate?
qa_highlights.answer: INR550 crore to be spent this year, with the INR165 crore oncology isolator line as a priority; brownfield or greenfield expansion is being planned.

qa_highlights.question: Constant-currency growth for the quarter on a consolidated basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15%. It explained the FX calculation uses the rate on each dispatch date, and guidance is set on a constant-currency basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is Cenexi turning around, and what is its profitability outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 EBITDA was about 4% margin, similar to the trend; management targets double-digit EBITDA by year-end. Q2 should beat last year because some quality releases slipped from Q1 because of the heat wave.

qa_highlights.question: GLP-1 scale-up and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: New line on track, with exhibit batches for several customers; transfers in the next 1-2 quarters. Revenue potential over 3 years is very limited; Canada launch could be upside.

qa_highlights.question: Are there patent-protected products in the CDMO base, and is the pipeline biologics or peptides?
qa_highlights.answer: No innovative products currently; some 505(b)(2) products have patents. Pipeline discussions are on peptides, not biologics. Biologics (Dr. Reddy's partnership) generate about INR50-60 crore a year.

543258|2026-03.headline: Indigo Paints Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 8.4% to INR397.9 crore; management signals margin sacrifice of 2-2.5pp to chase faster top-line growth.
543258|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 8.4% YoY to INR397.9 crore, with EBITDA of INR91.7 crore (23.0% margin) and gross margin of 48.6% versus 47.4% a year earlier, despite raw material costs rising 50-100% in March 2026 due to the Middle East conflict. PAT fell to INR57.3 crore (14.4% margin) as treasury income dropped to INR0.19 crore on mark-to-market losses. For FY26, standalone revenue grew 4.1% to INR1,330 crore and PAT excluding a one-off gratuity provision grew 4% to INR149.8 crore. Management said it will accept roughly 200-250bp lower gross margin, with EBITDA margin broadly unchanged, to accelerate top-line growth in FY27. It also said no major capex is planned until FY29, with the Jodhpur water-based plant commissioning in June 2026.

segments.commentary: Primers and distemper grew 14.9% value and 9.6% volume; putty and cement paint 12.6% value and 9.5% volume; emulsions 10.5% value and 11.2% volume; enamels and wood coatings 7.2% value and 5.4% volume. All four categories grew in value and volume.

segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR27.5 crore (+34.7% YoY); FY26 revenue INR75.1 crore (+17.8%). Gross margin around 40% plus/minus 1%. FY27 target is 30%-plus growth.

guidance_outlook: Management is prepared to accept a 2-2.5pp gross margin decline to drive faster top-line growth, while expecting EBITDA margin broadly unchanged.

Gross sales were growing double-digit for five consecutive months from November 2025, including March; the gap to reported net sales growth (8.5% in Q4) came from higher trade and influencer discounts netted off revenue.

Management said it is not guiding a specific net sales number for Q1 FY27 and expects net sales growth well above high-single-digit to low-double-digit levels over FY27, with the caveat that disruptions can set it back.
April growth was driven largely by price hikes; some dealer overstocking has occurred, so May-June demand is uncertain.
Industry price increases of about 12% on the overall basket were implemented; management does not foresee another significant price increase unless the Middle East situation deteriorates.

Apple Chemie targets 30%-plus revenue growth in FY27.
No major capex is envisaged until FY29; FCF is expected to step up from FY27 onwards. FY26 dividend proposed at INR5 per share, up 43% from INR3.5.
capex_capacity: Jodhpur water-based plant, 90,000 KL per annum capacity: final commissioning stage, trial production expected June 2026.
New solvent-based plant and expanded putty plant at Jodhpur have already commenced production in recent months.
Network at 31 March 2026: over 19,350 active dealers, over 12,200 tinting machines, 55 depots across all 28 states.
330 kW solar installation at Kochi factory is fully operational.
demand_pricing: Industry demand recovered from November 2025 after roughly 8 quarters of subdued growth; the Iran war from about March 2026 disrupted raw material supply and pushed some input prices up 50-100%.
The industry took about 12% price increases in three phases. Indigo's own unilateral price increase came around 24-25 March 2026, ahead of the market leader's 8 April increase.

Management said water-based paints are fully covered by price hikes; solvent-based enamels and wood coatings (about 17-18% of portfolio) have a small uncovered gap, partly offset by falling mineral turpentine oil prices.
Management said the competitive intensity has moderated over the last couple of quarters; it sees no change in behaviour since JSW's acquisition of Akzo.
Differentiated products make up about 30% of sales and are described as price-inelastic, so margin reduction is expected mainly in the other two-thirds of the portfolio.
Premium emulsions are a growing share; management said value growth has exceeded volume growth in almost all categories over the last 20 quarters or more.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Apple Chemie growth accelerate to 35% in Q4 and what are its margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was muted because government contractors' payments were delayed, but Q3 and Q4 grew about 30%-plus; gross margin is about 40% plus/minus 1%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company pursuing more aggressive market share gains, and will a 200bp gross margin sacrifice be enough to reach about 24% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: The Board judged the company had been too conservative on margins; it will spend more on trade schemes and influencers, lowering gross margin 2-2.5pp while EBITDA margin should hold. Management said yes, 24% growth is achievable.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the gross margin reduction come from, and is competition the reason?
qa_highlights.answer: Extra spend will be netted from revenue through trade discounts and influencer costs, mainly in non-differentiated products. Management said competitive intensity has normalised and the move reflects a wish to grow faster, not a response to competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Reconcile double-digit gross growth with single-digit reported growth, and will net sales be sacrificed?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross sales grew double-digit in each of the last five months, but higher trade and influencer discounts cut Q4 net growth to 8.5%. Management does not expect net sales growth to fall back to single digits.

qa_highlights.question: Will more price increases be needed, and how is pricing held if costs fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect another significant price increase unless the Middle East situation worsens. It said the company now acts independently on pricing and that margins should normalise by Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company growing in metros and dealer productivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Tier 1 and Tier 2 coverage is now good, and growth will come from deeper dealer throughput, not city size; with about 19,500 dealers it sees room to double sales per dealer.

543258|2026-06.headline: Indigo Paints Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 18.7% to INR350 crore with EBITDA margin up to 17.7%, its best Q1 margin in four years.
543258|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 18.7% YoY to INR350 crore, with double-digit volume and value growth across all four product categories. EBITDA rose 42% to INR61.9 crore (margin 17.7% vs 14.8%), and PAT rose 60.7% to INR42.4 crore, helped partly by a mark-to-market treasury gain. Consolidated revenue was INR369.7 crore (+19.7%), but subsidiary Apple Chemie's margins were compressed by high-cost inventory and limited B2B pass-through. Management said it will spend more aggressively on trade and influencers in Q2 to widen the growth gap versus the industry, and that the Jodhpur capex cycle is complete.

Solvent-based Jodhpur plant already in production for several months and ramping up.
Legacy water-based plant to be scrapped and output shifted to the new automated plant; opex expected to be broadly unchanged.

No significant capex planned for the next three years; free cash flow expected to improve versus the last five years.

Differentiated products are about 29% to 30% of revenue; management said the company is not planning new differentiated launches.
Competition: management said no meaningful change from JSW's acquisition of AkzoNobel or the Birla Opus entry.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Indigo not grown faster versus the market leader, and was the IPL advertising pause a missed opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said steep, frequent price hikes benefit the market leader most. The IPL pause was due to raw material uncertainty after the Iran war, not competitor ad intensity or Dhoni's playing status; it intends to put the money back in the coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Is July and August demand holding after Q1 upstocking, and is there a destocking risk for Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel overstocking was not seen at Indigo. July was a very good month with momentum maintained or slightly better than Q1; August was too early to call.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a price cut in H2, and what are the Q2 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: No further price hikes are planned for now. A price cut is possible, most likely after Diwali. No Q2 margin guidance was given; management suggested looking at the six-month period.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Jodhpur plant opex impact, and what is the competitive intensity after JSW-AkzoNobel?
qa_highlights.answer: The new plant replaces the legacy water-based plant with little opex change. Competitive intensity is unchanged, as JSW and AkzoNobel still operate separately.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new plant be ready for the festive season, and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Trial production is about 10 days away and should stabilise in about a month. The legacy plant is a backup. Management said gross margin may drop a couple of points, and EBITDA margin may move about 1 point either way.

543270|2026-03.headline: MTAR posted record Q4 FY26 sales of INR306 crore and FY26 revenue of INR876 crore (+30% YoY); FY27 guided to 80%+ growth and ~24% EBITDA margin.
543270|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue reached a record INR306 crore versus INR183 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of INR61.8 crore and PAT of about INR44.3 crore. Gross margin fell to 47.7% from 49.4%, which management attributed to input cost and freight pressure from geopolitical events and headcount added for expansion. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 80%+ (plus or minus 5%) with EBITDA margin of around 24%, and closing order book guidance of about INR5,000 crore by end-FY27. FY26 closed at INR2,580 crore order book, below the INR2,800 crore earlier guidance, which management attributed to nuclear and defence orders (about INR250 crore) slipping into the current quarter.

543270|2026-06.headline: MTAR Q1 FY27 revenue rose 130.4% YoY to INR360.7 crore with a 23.5% EBITDA margin; closing order book stated at INR5,143 crore.
543270|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR360.7 crore, up 130.4% YoY from INR156.6 crore, with EBITDA of INR85.1 crore (23.54% margin) and PAT of INR50.2 crore. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 80% revenue growth and a 24% ±100 bps EBITDA margin, and said it expects to do better. Working capital days fell sharply to 59 from 172 days for FY26, and management said debt is near nil after investments. Management highlighted civil nuclear order inflows, fuel cell capacity expansion in three phases, and a new data centre infrastructure product line.

segments.commentary: Highest-ever order inflow in the quarter for Kaiga 5 & 6; current nuclear order book about INR684 crore, with INR130-140 crore refurbishment orders expected in Q1 FY28 and about INR800 crore total nuclear book targeted. Execution of Kaiga 5 & 6 runs 1-3.5 years; refurbishment orders within 2 years; ramp-up starts H2 FY27.

segments.name: Clean Energy (fuel cells)
segments.commentary: Record order inflows in the quarter. Phase 1 capacity commissioned; Phase 2 due Sept-Oct 2026; Phase 3 (multifold expansion) due March 2027. Data centre infrastructure products entered; first batch of about INR45 crore for export due by March 2027.

segments.name: Aerospace and defence
segments.commentary: Management expects to double aerospace and defence revenue in FY27, with a 3-4 year ramp. Domestic defence opportunity above INR250 crore, including Tejas Mk-1A actuator assemblies (about INR140-150 crore program value). Oil & gas facility operational by October 2026.

segments.name: Products and others
segments.commentary: Revenue jumped to about INR100 crore in the quarter, roughly 50% of the Clean Energy run-rate per the analyst's framing; management says it will keep growing and H2 will be stronger than H1.

segments.name: Chemical Intermediates

543276|2026-03.headline: Craftsman guides FY27 revenue growth to mid-teens, with alloy wheel exit run-rate near 3 million wheels a year and net debt/EBITDA at 2.43x.

Sunbeam (aluminium) is being restructured through exits of unprofitable customers, product lines and a roughly INR30 crore low-value line sale, with benefits expected from Q2 FY27. Management guided FY27 revenue growth to mid-teens, conditional on aluminium prices holding near current levels. Rising manpower and capex costs were the main concerns, with the Gurgaon land sale and the DR Axion land deal also discussed.

543277|2026-03.headline: Laxmi Organic Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% QoQ with margins up in both businesses; FY26 revenue fell 6% YoY.

FY26 revenue declined 6% YoY, driven by feedstock deflation, margin pressure, a one-time Specialties impact and a lost large contract. Management described Middle East-driven spikes in acetic acid and methanol in March-April, with ETAC spreads moderating to about $150-160/t from a peak near $250. Dahej Phase 2 chemical charging is slated for Q1 FY27, with revenue contribution expected in H2 FY27, and Hitachi project output from Q3 FY27. Management declined to give absolute FY27/FY28 revenue numbers, citing market fluidity.

543278|2026-03.headline: Kalyan Jewellers Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT rose 118% YoY to INR410 crores on 66% revenue growth to INR10,275 crores.
543278|2026-03.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q4 FY26 was INR10,275 crores (up 66% YoY) and PAT was INR410 crores (up 118%), with India business PAT up 97% to INR366 crores. For FY26, consolidated revenue reached INR35,740 crores (up 43%) and PAT INR1,350 crores (up 89%). Management reported non-GML debt reduced by about INR360 crores in India, with non-GML now at INR300 crores, and Candere turned PAT positive in H2 FY26. Management said April 2026 started well despite a high base, while flagging Adhik Maas as a possible Q1 timing drag.

segments.name: Middle East

segments.name: Candere

Aim to make India non-GML debt zero in FY27, possibly by H1 FY27, but management declined to guide firmly on timing.

Management does not want to guide SSSG above 10% for the next 3-5 years, though recent SSSG has been 20-30%.

capex_capacity: Opened 129 showrooms across Kalyan and Candere in FY26, including the first Kalyan showroom in the UK.

Middle East: 2 new showrooms opened and 5-6 renovated into bigger formats; conversion of 4 FOCO stores to COCO worth about INR200-250 crores of inventory.
Q4 showroom count rose gross by 28 but net by about 4, with management saying only one small Madurai showroom closed and the rest were relocations.
Third regional brand launch in a South state delayed until post-election situation settles.
demand_pricing: Management said SSSG for the South was lower than for non-South in Q4; non-South acceleration continued from Q3.
Akshaya Tritiya sales grew strongly; coin sales were lower than estimated this year, unlike Dhanteras when they exceeded estimates.

Management said customers buy to a rupee budget, so volumes fall as gold prices rise; gold rose about 60-70% over the past year. Consumers were pushed to studded jewellery and lower karat (22K to 18K, 18K to 14K).
Management said gold supply is not a concern, with regular bank inventory and imports via GIFT City's India International Bullion Exchange.
Gold metal loan (GML) in India is capped by bank sanctions; Middle East GML is uncapped and rises with gold prices.
Management said inventory rises by only INR30-40 for every INR100 rise in gold price, to protect ROCE.

qa_highlights.question: Why did South SSSG diverge so sharply from non-South in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said South was lower, partly because its base is higher, and non-South acceleration continued from Q3 and was more pronounced in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will non-GML debt be fully repaid by H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to be non-GML debt free in FY27 and could do it by H1, but declined to guide on timing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost rise sequentially, and what is the underlying run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher processing charges and interest on advance tax explain the rise; about INR20 crores is one-off. Non-GML repayment should cut about INR30 crores in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 Adhik Maas period a risk to sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some sales may move between quarters, with possible slower days, but some purchases were preponed; April started well.

qa_highlights.question: How much of gross margin came from silver and platinum, and what is the FY27 impact?

Middle East franchise conversion and the Arab investor deal, which is not yet materialised.

Gold price-driven volume pressure and dependence on gold metal loan limits from banks.

543278|2026-06.headline: Kalyan Jewellers Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 38% to INR10,008 crore and PAT to INR349 crore, helped by a one-off customs duty gain.
543278|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue (net of bullion) grew 38% YoY to INR10,008 crore, with EBITDA of INR633 crore (vs INR508 crore) and PAT of INR349 crore (vs INR264 crore). India revenue rose to INR8,503 crore and Middle East to about INR1,320 crore, while Candere turned PAT positive at INR2.1 crore. Management attributed part of profit to a one-time customs duty gain of about INR40-41 crore that was passed to customers via old gold exchange offers, and flagged a 0.2-0.3% PBT margin dilution from exchange. Management said the PBT margin for the full year should hold at or above FY26 levels on a conservative basis.

segments.name: India (Kalyan)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR8,503 crore (+38% YoY) and EBITDA INR500 crore (+15%); PAT INR321 crore (+25%). Management said non-South markets now contribute 50-60% of revenue.

segments.name: Middle East
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR1,320 crore (+29%), EBITDA INR90 crore (vs INR73 crore), profit INR25 crore (vs INR22 crore).

segments.name: Candere (e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR141 crore (vs INR66 crore, roughly double); profit INR2.1 crore vs loss of INR10 crore. Management targets around 50 new Candere stores in FY27 and said Candere stays PAT positive for the year.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 PBT margin expected to be at least in line with FY26 on a conservative basis; exchange dilution of 0.2-0.3% to be offset by cash-for-gold, which is margin accretive.
Customs duty related gain expected at about INR60 crore in Q2 FY27, with some further benefit possible in the running quarter, though management said part may be shared with consumers.
Store expansion target unchanged: 84 Kalyan showrooms and about 50 Candere stores in FY27; H2 is typically heavier than H1. Management cites 70-80 showrooms a year overall.

Non-GML debt to be fully repaid by end-September 2026; second tranche of real estate collaterals to be released thereafter. Management said the company would be debt-free on a non-GML basis in a couple of months.
Recycled gold share to be maintained at 55-60% of revenue going forward.
Real estate sale: agreements signed for two land parcels for about INR102 crore; sale expected to close and proceeds received before end of Q1 FY27 (June quarter).
capex_capacity: Expansion is mainly franchise-led (FOCO model, where the franchisee funds capex and inventory and Kalyan runs the store for a margin share); franchisee ROCE cited at about 14%.
Kalyan ROCE rose to about 20% from the late teens; management expects further improvement from capital-light expansion.

New regional brand Akshaya Thanga Maligai (ATM) for Tamil Nadu: first showroom in Chennai on 21 August 2026, with four more showrooms planned in the following months, including other cities; expansion also to be predominantly FOCO.
Q1 FY27 saw 12 FOCO store openings, per the analyst's question; management confirmed no change to annual targets.
demand_pricing: Management described demand as robust except for about one month of Adhik Maas, when wedding demand slowed in parts of the country. Management said July demand was strong and continuing like Q1, but declined to quantify the trend.
Gold prices corrected about 15-20% over 2-3 months; management said customers buy by budget, so volumes rise when prices fall.
Recycled gold ('Shine with India' campaign) rose to over 46% of revenue in Q1, with June above 55%, as oil-driven forex pressure pushed the company to reduce imported gold.
Cash-for-gold (new product) grew from single-digit share in Q1 to double-digit share as of the call; management said peers are also adopting it.

Exchange transactions are priced at the board rate; cash purchases of old gold are at a discount to spot, which management said is margin accretive. Bullion sales in Q1 were used to fund cash needs of vendors, mainly studded vendors on invoice basis.
Employee cost rose about 54% YoY standalone; management said this is more than the usual annual increment and worth about 0.2-0.3% of revenue, offset by operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any bonus issue planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no bonus share plans as of now.

qa_highlights.question: Ex the one-off gain of INR410 crore, standalone PBT growth was only about 14%, so what drove the margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PBT margin ex-bullion was about 5.1% vs 5.5-5.6% earlier. The gain was partly passed to consumers via exchange offers (INR30-40 crore), exchange dilutes margin by 0.2-0.3%, and platinum/silver one-offs of about 0.2% were absent.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 0.2-0.3% exchange-related dilution persist for the next two to three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no for full year: cash-for-gold should offset exchange dilution, and it expects FY27 PBT margin at least in line with FY26 on a conservative basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is the gold price fall boosting volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said customers come with a budget, so lower gold prices mechanically raise volumes; wedding demand cannot pause more than 2-3 weeks, and discretionary demand may pause about 1-1.5 months.

qa_highlights.question: How much customs duty benefit is expected in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR60 crore in Q2, with some benefit possible in the running quarter but part to be shared with consumers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Candere?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Candere has been PAT positive since 2H FY26, will stay positive in FY27, and will add about 50 stores with focus on inventory throughput in existing stores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the employee cost increase one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not one-time; it is above the usual annual increment, occurs once every few years, and operating leverage should absorb it.

risks_watch: Margin: exchange-led volumes dilute PBT margin by 0.2-0.3%; the full-year margin target depends on cash-for-gold scaling up.
One-off customs duty gains (about INR41 crore in Q1, about INR60 crore expected in Q2) may not recur and partly go to consumers.
Gold price volatility (15-20% correction) may pause discretionary demand and push customers to change grammage/price points.
Employee cost up about 54% YoY standalone; watch whether operating leverage offsets it.
Execution of non-GML debt repayment by September 2026 and the real estate sale proceeds.
Management declined to comment on governance questions raised in the press about related-party transactions; an open overhang for investors.
ATM's ramp-up and whether the regional format can scale beyond the first five stores.

543279|2026-03.headline: Suryoday SFB FY26 PAT rose to ₹152 crores from ₹115 crores; management targets FY27 PAT above ₹300 crores, with credit cost guided at 70-80 bps.
543279|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of disciplined execution and gradual stabilisation after elevated microfinance credit costs. Q4 showed improvement: inclusive finance slippages fell to about ₹74 crores from ₹116 crores in Q3 (the call also cited ₹106 crores on a total-bank basis), and monthly disbursements returned to about ₹500 crores. FY26 net total income rose 10.2% to ₹1,458 crores and PAT to ₹152 crores, with GNPA at 6.5% (₹864 crores) and CRAR at 20.5%. Management guided to 30%+ growth, a 1.2% ROA for Q1 FY27 rising to 1.6% by Q4, and a cost-to-income ratio of 67-68%.

financial_highlights.value: ₹542 crores, of which ₹508 crores receivable from CGFMU

financial_highlights.metric: Mortgage book incl. micro home loans (Mar'26)

segments.name: Inclusive finance (microfinance)
segments.commentary: Shifting from JLG to individual Vikas loans, now 75% of the inclusive finance portfolio and growing about 40-45% YoY. Current-book collection efficiency is about 99.7%; slippages were about ₹74 crores in Q4 versus ₹116 crores in Q3.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Portfolio ₹1,819 crores, up 36% YoY. Stress is concentrated in an Odisha pocket; management says ex-Odisha metrics are about 2x better than market CV stress.

segments.name: Mortgages and micro home loans
segments.commentary: Mortgage book ₹3,013 crores, up 38% YoY. Stress in older mortgage and MHL portfolios in Karnataka was about 4% of the portfolio, with a few high-ticket LAP cases (₹3 crores+) in SARFAESI resolution.

segments.commentary: Credit on UPI outstanding about ₹200 crores with 97-98% of dues paid; 90+ DPD about 1.5%. Of 10 lakh prequalified customers, about 5.5 lakh sanctioned and about 3 lakh utilised.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 ROA guided at about 1.2%, rising to 1.6% by Q4 FY27; Q4 FY26 ROA was 1.1%.
FY27 PAT target above ₹300 crores (about 2x FY26), per management's presentation.
FY27 credit cost of about 1%, per CFO earlier in the call; later revised to 70-80 bps for the coming year (FY27) in response to a follow-up question.
Cost-to-income ratio of 67-68% for FY27, with a stated goal of staying below 70%.
Quarterly slippages targeted at ₹75-90 crores; GNPA guided to about 3% for FY27 with CGFMU claims and write-offs as the main drivers.
NIM to be range-bound at 8-9%, with an uptick possible as the paying book grows; current NIM about 50 bps suppressed. Growth targeted at 20-30% of asset size.
capex_capacity: CGFMU claims: about ₹510 crores claimable, of which about ₹450 crores (up to ₹475 crores) is expected in FY27; the first cohort claim is targeted for Q1 or Q2, with the FY25 cohort the largest.
CGFMU cover premium expected at about ₹100-110 crores for FY27 (about ₹23 crores per quarter currently).
Fundraise: Tier 2 is the likely first step, possibly within FY27. An equity raise is more contingent, given the stock trades below book (P/B under 1) and the need to protect incumbent shareholders.
Branch expansion is kept rationalised and low-cost; corporate headcount is held flat, with hiring concentrated in frontline roles.
demand_pricing: Digital deposits are about 50% of net incremental deposit flows, with average ticket about ₹1.25 lakh and at least two deposits per customer on average.
Cost of funds has hardened; elevated Q4 rates have not come down as in prior years. The bank uses a mix of deposits and refinancing lines to manage funding.
Management sees unmet demand as large, especially where smaller MFIs have exited; the top 10-15 MFIs hold about 19% market share.
Individual-loan ticket sizes are being raised selectively; tenor is moving toward 3 years for high-ticket loans, with a portion above ₹1 lakh under review.

qa_highlights.question: Given the stronger Q4 performance, is the 1.2% Q1 ROA target realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said yes: the paying book is higher entering Q1, impaired book should exit on CGFMU claims, and Q1 typically has the most PSLC sales.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state slippage level and retail-asset (RA) slippage guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said RA slippage could settle near 1.25% over the next two halves as CV Odisha stress and high-ticket mortgage cases are resolved. Bank-wide slippages are targeted at ₹75-90 crores a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the CGFMU claim will be filed, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹510 crores is claimable, with ₹450 crores expected in FY27 and the timing (Q1 or Q2) still open. None filed in April; May is unlikely.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the bank raising capital, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bank is raising capital to sustain 30%+ growth, with CRAR around 20% as the internal comfort level. Tier 2 is most likely first, and an equity raise is subject to shareholder considerations.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided NIM to 8-9% and agreed NIM is suppressed by about 50 bps, with an uptick expected as non-paying assets convert to paying.

qa_highlights.question: What credit cost should be expected for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided FY27 credit cost to 70-80 bps. Management also said downside risk from the Middle East war and diesel prices would be watched, with CV impact only if diesel rises above 10-15%.
