543279|2026-06.headline: Suryoday SFB Q1 FY27: GNPA 6.5%, NNPA 1.2% after INR387 crore CGFMU claim; ROA about 1.6% helped by INR46 crore PSL income.
543279|2026-06.overview: Gross advances rose 32.5% YoY to INR14,376 crore and deposits rose 29.4% YoY to INR14,634 crore in Q1 FY27. Bank-level slippages fell to INR92 crore from INR106 crore QoQ, and MFI slippages fell to INR53 crore from INR73 crore. Other income was lifted by about INR90 crore of PSL/other income plus INR46 crore of PSL certificate sales (INR1,600 crore sold), which management said will not recur at this scale in Q2 and Q3. Management reiterated FY27 guidance: credit cost 0.8–1.0%, ROE 13–14% range, ROA of about 1.6% by Q4, and cost-to-income of 67–70%.

financial_highlights.change: Adjusted for INR134 crore CGFMU receivable: 2.9% / 0.3%

financial_highlights.value: Down about 8 bps QoQ; guided ~7.5% for rest of FY27

segments.name: Inclusive finance (MFI/JLG and individual loans)
segments.commentary: Current-bucket collection efficiency 99.2%, recent-cohort 99.4%. Individual loans are about 80% of monthly onboarding; IF share of advances fell to 44% from 48%. Slippages run below INR20 crore a month.

segments.name: Vehicle finance (CV)
segments.commentary: PAR rose to 11.5% from 10.1% QoQ, attributed to fuel prices and load availability. About 75–80% of the book is used CVs. Management expects normalisation from Q2/Q3 after monsoon.

segments.name: Mortgages and secured retail
segments.commentary: Secured retail growing 30–35% YoY. Mortgages present in under 25% of branches, targeted at 40–45% by year-end. Some mortgage slippages are being resolved through legal process.

segments.name: Digital (CLOU/UPI credit line, digital deposits, digital MSME)
segments.commentary: Digital deposits INR2,222 crore with average daily accretion of INR6 crore. UPI credit customers crossed 9 lakh; CLOU convenience fee income INR18 crore against about INR13 crore related cost. Digital MSME disbursements INR59 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 credit cost guided at 0.8–1.0%; Q1 at 0.8%.
Cost of funds around 7.5% for the rest of FY27; NIM expected to stay similar to the Q1 level.
ROA guided at about 1.6% in Q4 FY27 with no change to the start-of-year guidance; management said Q2 PSL income will be lower.
Steady-state ROE 13–14%, with a target of 0.5–1% YoY improvement over the next couple of years.
PSL income guided at INR10–15 crore in each of Q2 and Q3, and INR15–20 crore in Q4.

Opex (full-stack cost-to-income) target 67–70%; PAT guidance of INR300 crore-plus for FY27 referenced by an analyst; management said Q2 would be subdued, with about INR75 crore per quarter as the focus.
Yield on advances to stabilise at 17.2–17.5%; no immediate pricing change planned this quarter.
Capital adequacy about 20%, with a target of 20–22%. Fresh Tier 2 raise being explored with a target to close in Q2; Tier 1 raise under evaluation.
capex_capacity: About 50 branches to be added in Q2 and Q3 FY27, mainly for IF and CV expansion into new locations.
Mortgage presence to rise from under 25% of branches to 40–45% by year-end.

CLOU customer base about 6 lakh active users, with 9–10 lakh approved. Target to double active users to about 12 lakh this fiscal year. Onboarding 1.5–2 lakh customers a month, average ticket under INR5,000.
Remaining CGFMU claim of about INR15–20 crore due this year; a further INR135–150 crore claimable in subsequent years.
demand_pricing: Management said the MFI cycle has turned, but it is staying cautious on growth and will not treat the recovery as a reason to grow aggressively.
Advances are growing faster than deposits; MFI performing book grew about INR500 crore in one quarter.
IBPC funding reopened at roughly 5% after the MFI book improved.
Deposit costs: SA cost of funds 5.5% (from 5.7%); FD cost about 8.1%. FD rates have not eased.
VL (individual loan) yield about 25–25.25%; secured assets yield about 12%.
Management said the competition will be intense and the digital play is the differentiator.

qa_highlights.question: Other income of about INR147 crore looks high. What is the steady-state run-rate for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income included about INR90 crore of PSL income plus INR46 crore from selling INR1,600 crore of PSL certificates. Q2 and Q3 PSL income is expected at INR10–15 crore each, and Q4 at INR15–20 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 1.6% ROA reach 1.8–1.9% by Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 included about INR40 crore of PSL income, and the next two quarters will not have similar PSL opportunities, so the 1.6% ROA is not a base for linear increase.

qa_highlights.question: What happened to yield on non-NPA advances (17.2% to 16.1%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix shift away from IF (share down from 48% to 44%) cost about INR0.75 impact, and Q4 had higher MFI recovery income. Yield is expected to return to about 17%, and the stabilised range is 17.2–17.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did slippages stay elevated and what is the resolution path?
qa_highlights.answer: Bank-level slippages fell to INR92 crore from INR106 crore. Some mortgage cases are being resolved through legal process, and management expects these to come down in the coming quarter with well-collateralised assets.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CV PAR rise to 11.5% from 10.1%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the increase to higher fuel prices and load availability, with monsoon seasonality also adding to it. It expects PAR to settle back by Q2 and normalise by about September, and it has no geographic concentration in the book.

qa_highlights.question: Is the insurance model at risk if many lenders take cover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said insurance is a last-resort backstop and the bank is not using it as a shield for business. Norms will be tighter and premiums may exceed claims in the next couple of years; NCGTC is described as well funded.

risks_watch: CV PAR at 11.5% (from 10.1%) driven by fuel prices and load availability; monitor whether it normalises in Q2.
Deposit growth of about 30% with CASA held at 21% and FD costs about 8.1%; deposit roll-overs may reprice lower but are a constraint.
Dependence on one-off PSL income and CGFMU claims for profitability; the remaining claim is small, but about INR135–150 crore is claimable later.
Rising inflation and geopolitical disruption were flagged as possible pressure on collections, though management said stress is not expected in the next six months.
Tier 1 capital raise not finalised; Tier 2 raise was expected to close this quarter.
543279|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on asset quality and collections, but cautious on growth and the MFI cycle. Management was explicit that Q2 will be weaker because PSL income falls away, and it did not commit to a higher ROE. On the CV PAR and the insurance-claim questions, answers were detailed and specific.
key_quotes: It is extremely important that we do not really take this as a reveal of the cycle and go aggressive.
The focus is at whatever we do, can every improvement be sustainable quarter-on-quarter?
We are not really to kind of guiding higher ROE at this point of time.

rows.why: Yield on non-NPA advances fell to 16.1% from 17.2%, cost of funds is guided at about 7.5% with NIM similar to Q1, PSL income drops to INR10-20 crore a quarter from about INR90 crore, and FD costs of about 8.1% have not eased.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 50 branches to be added in Q2 and Q3 FY27 for IF and CV expansion, and mortgage presence to rise from under 25% of branches to 40-45% by year-end, so the branch network is growing on a firm plan.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Gross advances grew 32.5% YoY to INR14,376 crore and deposits 29.4% to INR14,634 crore, with the MFI performing book up about INR500 crore in one quarter, although management is cautious on growth.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 credit cost at 0.8-1.0% and ROA at about 1.6% by Q4, and said the 1.6% ROA is not a base for linear increase to 1.8-1.9%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management said Q2 will be weaker as PSL income falls to INR10-15 crore from about INR90 crore in Q1, and CV PAR rose to 11.5% from 10.1%, though it expects normalisation by about September.

rows.label: Tier 2 capital raise to close in Q2
rows.why: Capital adequacy is about 20% against a 20-22% target, and a fresh Tier 2 raise is being explored with a target close in Q2, while the Tier 1 raise is still under evaluation.

rows.label: CGFMU claims inflow
rows.why: About INR15-20 crore of the CGFMU claim is due this year and a further INR135-150 crore is claimable in later years, though the remaining claim is small against the INR387 crore claimed in Q1.

rows.label: CLOU digital credit scale-up
rows.why: Target to double CLOU active users from about 6 lakh to about 12 lakh this fiscal, with onboarding of 1.5-2 lakh customers a month and CLOU fee income of INR18 crore against about INR13 crore cost in Q1.

tone.note: Management was confident on asset quality, collections and the IF cycle turn, but cautious on growth, explicit that Q2 is weaker as PSL income falls away, and did not commit to a higher ROE; analysts pushed on the 1.6% ROA path, the yield drop to 16.1%, and the CV PAR rise to 11.5%.

543280|2026-03.headline: Nazara FY26 EBITDA rose 66% to INR 255 crore, with Q4 EBITDA margin at 19.5%, helped by a one-time INR 31 crore Rusk Media gain.
543280|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue was INR 1,829 crore (up 13% YoY) and EBITDA INR 255 crore (up 66%), a record, with EBITDA margin at 13.9%. Q4 revenue was INR 398 crore and EBITDA INR 78 crore (19.5% margin). Gaming rose to 90% of EBITDA in FY26 from 56% in FY25. Bluetile and BestPlay acquisition was completed in the quarter but will be consolidated only from Q1 FY27, pending Spanish FDI approval expected in 3-4 weeks. Management guided to growth in revenue and EBITDA for FY27 without numerical guidance.

financial_highlights.value: INR 261 crore, EBITDA INR 101 crore (39% margin)
financial_highlights.change: revenue broadly flat YoY per analyst

financial_highlights.change: from INR 14 crore loss in FY25
sequential decline of about 24% due to NODWIN deconsolidation
includes one-time INR 31 crore gain on Rusk Media

segments.name: Mobile gaming
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 713 crore (+38%) and EBITDA INR 137 crore (+33%), driven by LiveOps, user acquisition and data analytics under the COE model. Kiddopia returned to subscriber growth in Q3 and continued in Q4; Animal Jam expanded margins.

segments.name: PC and console publishing (Curve Games, Fusebox, Human Fall Flat)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 261 crore and EBITDA INR 101 crore (39% margin). Human Fall Flat crossed 58 million lifetime units. Analyst noted revenue growth was hardly visible YoY; management said the company had a low signing period before the acquisition.

segments.name: Offline gaming (Smaaash, Funky Monkeys)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 99 crore and EBITDA INR 27 crore, profitable in the year. Funky Monkeys footprint expanding; Smaaash 2.0 format in progress.

segments.commentary: Revenue and EBITDA each grew 32% YoY in FY26, but Q4 revenue declined sequentially, which management attributed to exiting traditional adtech and UK new-homes market weakness.

segments.name: Sportskeeda
segments.commentary: Remained profitable in FY26 despite Google Core update traffic losses; analyst cited revenue down about 38% in FY26. Management expects margin improvement in FY27 on a smaller base.

segments.name: NODWIN (associate)
segments.commentary: EBITDA swung to INR 21 crore profit in FY26 from INR 14 crore loss in FY25. Q4 associate losses included a INR 50 crore goodwill write-off on OML assets, mainly NH7 Weekender. Planning to raise USD 100-200 million and an independent IPO.

guidance_outlook: No numerical guidance; management expects growth in both revenue and EBITDA in FY27, with operating leverage from COEs and AI.

Bluetile consolidation from Q1 FY27 once Spanish FDI approval is received (expected in 3-4 weeks). Management said pro forma EBITDA would at least double if combined with Bluetile's CY25 EBITDA of INR 254 crore.
Curve Games expects at least 6 new releases in FY27, maybe more; margin target of 50% on signed games.
Fusebox plans three Big Brother seasons and a Traitors launch in FY27, plus three new Love Island seasons.
Non-core divestments (NODWIN, Sportskeeda or adtech) possible in FY27-FY28; management said there is no rush.
Sportskeeda margins expected to increase in FY27 on a smaller revenue base.

Curve Games plans to increase development spend to build its release pipeline.
Smaaash 2.0 re-imagined format in progress; Funky Monkeys footprint expanding.
Animal Jam: first Mattel Monster High IP integration launched in Q1 FY27; Roblox native experience planned; a new hyper-casual game for kids and women in North America is due in Q2 FY27.
demand_pricing: Bluetile operates in casual evergreen (solitaire, word games, board and puzzle games) and hybrid casual. Management cited Triple Dot (valued over USD 1 billion) and Easybrain (acquired by Miniclip for about USD 1 billion) as comparables.
Management said platform commissions (Google, Apple at 30%) are coming down over time, which should aid margins.
Adtech decline reflects a deliberate shift from traditional adtech to the DSP product Vizibl; UK new-homes market weakness hit Space and Time's Q4 discretionary spend.
Fusebox revenue is seasonal; Q3 FY26 fell about 49% QoQ before recovering in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR 51 crore other income and what explains the NODWIN associate loss of about INR 31 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income included a one-time INR 31 crore gain on Rusk Media from a revaluation after its new funding round, plus currency gains on loans to Nazara UK and mutual fund gains. The associate loss reflected a INR 50 crore NODWIN goodwill write-off on OML assets and Moonshine losses.

qa_highlights.question: Is Sportskeeda's decline recoverable, or should margins be modelled at 12-15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said recovery has not yet come through; the focus in FY26 was protecting EBITDA over revenue. Cost optimisation continues and margins are expected to rise in FY27 on a smaller base. Pro Football Network and PrimeTimer are showing positive signs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NODWIN fundraising and IPO plan, and will Nazara monetise its stake?
qa_highlights.answer: NODWIN plans to raise USD 100-200 million, a mix of primary and secondary, and prepare an independent IPO as soon as timing is right. Nazara will consider monetising non-core assets (NODWIN, Sportskeeda or adtech) but is in no hurry.

qa_highlights.question: What is Bluetile's TAM and scalability, and what is the FY27 growth and margin outlook post consolidation?
qa_highlights.answer: Bluetile's casual evergreen and hybrid casual segments were described as large and profitable with global reach. Management gave no specific guidance but pointed to Bluetile CY25 revenue of INR 1,460 crore and EBITDA of INR 254 crore, with combined EBITDA at least doubling pro forma.

qa_highlights.question: Why did adtech revenue decline sequentially in Q4, and is it temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline was partly deliberate, exiting traditional adtech, and partly UK new-homes market weakness hitting Space and Time. Space and Time finished FY26 ahead of AOP and management expects FY27 growth.

qa_highlights.question: Can Curve Games margins hold above 30-35% as Switch 2 launches scale, and when will Bluetile consolidate?
qa_highlights.answer: Curve targets 50% margin on signed games and expects margins to hold. Bluetile is expected to close after Spanish FDI approval in 3-4 weeks and consolidate from Q1 FY27.

risks_watch: Q4 other income (INR 51 crore) includes a one-time INR 31 crore Rusk Media gain; underlying earnings are lower.
Sportskeeda is still hit by Google Core update traffic losses; FY26 revenue fell about 38% per analyst.
PC and console publishing revenue was almost flat in FY26 at INR 261 crore; Curve's new-release pipeline must convert.
Bluetile consolidation depends on Spanish FDI approval timing; deal must close before FY27 numbers are included.
Fusebox seasonality remains; Q3 FY26 saw about 49% QoQ decline.
AdTech revenue declined sequentially in Q4 FY26, with UK new-homes weakness.
Monetisation of non-core assets and NODWIN's independent IPO have no set timelines.

key_quotes: FY '26 was a pivotal year for Na zara. Revenue reached INR 1,829 crores and EBITDA grew 66% to INR 255 crores, our highest ever, with Q4 EBITDA margins reaching 19.5%, - almost doubling on a year -on-year basis.

543280|2026-06.headline: Nazara Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR 429 crore and EBITDA INR 46 crore, with a PAT loss of INR 82 crore; Bluetile/BestPlay acquisition restructured to $303 million all-cash.
543280|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR 429 crore and EBITDA INR 46 crore, with a PAT loss of INR 82 crore driven by associate losses (about INR 62 crore share of loss) and impairment, mainly on the Moonshine remnant value. Excluding NODWIN's deconsolidation, comparable revenue grew about 9% YoY. Gaming revenue rose 14% YoY to INR 275 crore at a 19.5% EBITDA margin, with heavier user acquisition spend compressing margins at Bluetile, Kiddopia and Curve. Management restructured the Bluetile and BestPlay deal to a fixed $303 million all-cash price, with $89 million at closing and $214 million by 1 April 2027, and named Bluetile founder Raymond Stauffer as Nazara CEO from 1 September 2026.

financial_highlights.change: Largely share of associate losses and impairment

financial_highlights.value: INR 518 crore revenue, INR 55 crore EBITDA
INR 53 crore, EBITDA INR 14 crore (27% margin)

segments.name: Kiddopia / Animal Jam
segments.commentary: Kiddopia revenue grew 19% YoY on higher UA spend with 24-month LTV/CAC trending up; Animal Jam revenue grew 11% YoY.

segments.name: Fusebox Games
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 82 crore, up 12% YoY; Love Island ranked #1 in free apps and #5 in top-grossing apps in the US. Big Brother and The Traitors are the next growth drivers.

segments.name: Curve Games (PC and Console publishing)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 53 crore and EBITDA INR 14 crore (27% margin), down from about 40% last financial year; more than 60% of development spend went to new signings and releases start from Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Offline gaming (SMAAASH, Funky Monkeys)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 34 crore and EBITDA INR 11 crore (33% margin); Funky Monkeys revenue grew 58% YoY. SMAAASH 2.0 first reinvention targeted at Lower Parel, Mumbai, in Q4 FY27.

segments.commentary: Datawrkz revenue INR 126 crore with EBITDA INR 3 crore. Management said 60-80% of AdTech revenue is pass-through, so revenue growth does not translate directly into EBITDA.

segments.name: Absolute Sports (Sportskeeda, Pro Football Network)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 28 crore and EBITDA INR 1 crore; Sportskeeda turned EBITDA positive on lower costs, and Pro Football Network posted a 19% EBITDA margin versus break-even in Q1 FY26.

segments.name: NODWIN Gaming
segments.commentary: Q1 is the seasonally weakest quarter with stable revenue and losses substantially lower YoY; organic growth target 30%+ for FY27, with IPO readiness in progress and Comic Con expanding to 14 Indian events.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Jawar (AK Investment) asked Bluetile's founder journey and whether growth was organic or inorganic, and what skin in the game Raymond Stauffer would have under the all-cash deal.
qa_highlights.answer: Raymond was not on the call; Maxime Loppin said Bluetile's growth is not organic in the sense of inorganic M&A but is driven by paid UA, with spend based on campaign ROI on new games and features. On incentives, Nitish Mittersain said a structure to incentivise management including Raymond would be communicated over the next few days, with the fundraise not discussed before Board approval.

qa_highlights.question: Samarth Patel (Equirus) asked about the Curve Games release slate, margin trajectory, and offline capex.
qa_highlights.answer: Susan Planck said releases start with Sovereign Tower (this week), Dragon Shelter (September 2026) and more unannounced titles before year-end; Q1 27% margin is below the ~40% of last year and new signings should lift later quarters. Nitish Mittersain said offline commitment across SMAAASH and Funky Monkeys is about INR 50 crore, with SMAAASH 2.0 Lower Parel launch expected January-March 2027 and no further capital decided until product-market fit.

qa_highlights.question: Samarth Patel asked about NODWIN's IPO progress and whether a NODWIN secondary sale would fund the Bluetile consideration.
qa_highlights.answer: Akshat Rathee said Comic Con expands from 11 shows last year to 14 domestic plus 2-3 international, and pre-IPO interest is strong. Nitish Mittersain said funding options include about $20 million of cash on Bluetile's balance sheet, internal cash flow, debt, equity and stake sales, without confirming a NODWIN secondary.

qa_highlights.question: Kunal Bajaj (Choice) asked whether the EBITDA margin decline would normalise quickly, why Bluetile margin fell, D&A outlook, and the timing of the $214 million tranches.
qa_highlights.answer: Nitish Mittersain said margins are deferred as UA is expensed upfront with no caps while LTV/CAC guardrails hold; Bluetile's Q1 margin is about 11% versus 17.6% a year ago. D&A outside Bluetile is steady; Bluetile's amortisation was not quantified. 543280|2026-09.headline: Nazara Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR 803 crore (up 53% YoY) and EBITDA rose 93% to INR 120 crore, helped by Bluetile and BestPlay consolidation from 1 August 2026.
543280|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the first quarter including Bluetile and BestPlay, consolidated from 1 August 2026, and Nazara reported record revenue of INR 803 crore with EBITDA margin up 311 bps to 14.9%. Gaming is now 82% of revenue and effectively all EBITDA before corporate costs. Organic gaming growth was modest at 11% revenue and 17% EBITDA, with the acquired mobile businesses doing most of the lifting. Management, under a new CEO, CFO and Executive Director, framed the next year around platform centres of excellence, AI adoption and gaming focus, and declined to give numerical growth targets. Non-core assets (NODWIN, AdTech, Absolute Sports and others) are to be monetised opportunistically.

segments.name: Mobile gaming (incl. Bluetile and BestPlay)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 550 crore (up 167% YoY) and EBITDA INR 103 crore (up 151%). Bluetile and BestPlay contributed INR 329 crore revenue and INR 64 crore EBITDA in their first two months under Nazara; Aug-Sep margin was about 19.5% per the analyst, versus about 10.5% in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Mobile studios (organic)
segments.commentary: WildWorks revenue up 41% and EBITDA up 39% on Animal Jam content. Kiddopia revenue up 21% with subscribers at 5% and ARPU at $7.94 (up 8%), but EBITDA fell on higher user acquisition. Fusebox revenue down 4% on lower organic installs while EBITDA rose 7%.

segments.name: PC and console (Curve)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 77 crore (up 27%) and EBITDA INR 30 crore (up 61%), margin 38.9% versus 30.8%. Drivers were Sovereign Tower, the mobile debut of Wobbly Life and Human: Fall Flat, which has passed 60 million players.

segments.name: Offline gaming (Funky Monkeys, SMAAASH)
segments.commentary: Revenue flat at INR 29 crore, EBITDA up 29% to INR 8 crore. Funky Monkeys opened 10 stores in the last 12 months and plans 5 more in FY27. SMAAASH 2.0 launch is slightly delayed pending regulatory approvals.

segments.name: AdTech (Datawrkz, Space & Time)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 124 crore and EBITDA INR 0.8 crore. Management expects a temporary H2 dip as an anchor client restructures and pauses ad spend.

segments.name: Sports and media (Absolute Sports, Pro Football Network, Sportskeeda)
segments.commentary: Absolute Sports revenue INR 23 crore with adjusted EBITDA INR 1.7 crore. Pro Football Network revenue up 20% with EBITDA margin of 17% (versus -18%). Sportskeeda operating costs down 13% QoQ, with syndication revenue partly offsetting lower ad rates.

segments.name: NODWIN (associate)
segments.commentary: Not reported in the update. H1 revenue and EBITDA are roughly flat; two IPs (I-Popstar and All That Matters) slipped from Q2 to Q3. The Rs 23 crore share of loss in Q2 reflects an EBITDA loss plus an impairment on the Turkish investee Publishme. Pre-IPO round and IPO are being prepared.

543283|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated SSSG rose to 14.4% (Q3: 8.2%) with dine-in volumes up ~43%, and management targets 9-10% pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin in FY27.
543283|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's strongest operating quarter in recent history, with consolidated revenue of INR360 crores (+23.1% YoY) and every segment and channel growing at double-digit rates. Growth was entirely volume-led with no price increase in Q4, while gross margin fell about 300 bps YoY to 65.5% due to segment mix, value campaigns in weaker dayparts and Middle East input inflation. Management says gross margin bottomed in February 2026 and recovered about 100 bps in March and April. Net debt was about INR100-102 crores, and FY27 guidance includes 40 new restaurants, around INR140 crores of capex and a 9-10% pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin.

Back-end cost to fall from 7.1% to ~6.5% of revenue in FY27 and ~6% over the longer term.

Management said FY27 full-year revenue growth of 22-25% is reasonable if SSSG is double-digit and store expansion is 12-13% (answered 'on a full year basis, yes').
capex_capacity: FY26: 35 new restaurants added (14 in Q4), taking network to 262; 32 net additions versus 14 net in the prior two years combined.

qa_highlights.question: Is double-digit SSSG for FY27 achievable given the cautious tone on H2 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects early double-digit SSSG comfortably and that the internal aim is to cross double-digit full-year SSSG, while declining to give formal guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 9-10% margin target be achieved from the current base, and is the 100-150 bps gross margin recovery net of inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 67-68% gross margin range is after inflation; gross margin gap to FY25 peak of 68.5% is now ~3 pp and expected to narrow to ~1-1.5 pp. Gross margin rose in March and April despite LPG price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q4 new-store drag on margins persist?

qa_highlights.question: Why did premium CDR margins fall sharply from Q3 to Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to new restaurants (4 opened in Q4), seasonality (December peak in Q3), one-time setup and liquor costs, and newer markets (Mumbai, Delhi) that take time to build up; mature cohort margins are fine.

qa_highlights.question: How will store expansion avoid the closures seen in FY23?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some Tier 2/3 stores were closed in FY23 but its current operating model works in those markets; FY27 plan of 40 stores is ~15% of the base and comparable to the 35 added in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for International given Middle East disruption and currency effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Two of ~8 restaurants (Bahrain, Dubai) are impacted; both improved month-on-month in April and May. No new Middle East sites reviewed in the last three months; focus is on Southeast Asia.

qa_highlights.question: What is the company's per-restaurant revenue and peak capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said peak-day capacity is not a constraint: a 4-session day at 100 seats gives 400 covers, about INR9 crores a month at INR750 per cover, and the company will open nearby stores 5-7 km apart when demand grows.

543300|2026-03.headline: Sona Comstar Q4 FY26 revenue rose 47% YoY to ₹1,272 crore, a record quarter, though EBITDA margin fell 2.7pp to 24.4%.
543300|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 posted record revenue (₹1,272 crore, +47% YoY), record EBITDA (₹311 crore, +32%) and record PAT (₹192 crore, +17%), with BEV revenue of ₹359 crore at a record 39% share. Margins compressed on commodity inflation with pass-through lag, product mix (lower-margin traction motors and railways) and a PLI income base effect. Management won four new driveline orders, including three from European OEMs in one quarter, and said Europe's EV order flow is returning. Full-year FY26 revenue grew 26% to ₹4,475 crore, with EBITDA margin at 24.7% and adjusted PAT up 11%.

segments.commentary: Traction motors about 10% of revenue. Suspension motors expected to grow 3-4x in FY27 volumes, reaching single digit share of revenue in FY26 and possibly double digits in FY27.

segments.name: Differential gears and assemblies
segments.commentary: Legacy products kept growing alongside new products. Q4 saw 7 non-EV differential gear programs from existing customers worth about ₹3 billion.

segments.name: Railway (acquired)
segments.commentary: Lower-margin, high-return business, consolidated during FY26 and funded with about ₹1,800 crore. Q4 approvals for electric control panels (first batch supplied) and HVAC (supply to start this quarter).

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Eastern markets were 60% of Q4 revenue vs 40% a year earlier. India exceeded 50% of mix for full year FY26.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin band guided at 23-25% post railway acquisition, replacing the earlier 24-26% band for the core business.
Commodity inflation (steel, aluminium, copper, freight, packaging, energy) expected to keep pressuring margins in the foreseeable future, as pass-through lags.
Haryana minimum wage hike effective 1 April 2026 expected to add labour cost; to be offset via productivity, tighter headcount addition and workload management.
Novelic India SOP for one customer expected at end of calendar 2026; Europe in-cabin safety NCAP requirement moved to 2027.

Railway growth over 3-5 years framed through capacity/process improvement, white-space variants and new products (HVAC needs about 3 years for full rolling stock coverage; electric panels 12-15 months).
capex_capacity: FY26 capex ₹369 crore; additional land bought for about ₹110 crore.
Gas requirement cut by nearly 20% at company level via electric heating, gas-flow optimisation and process changes; no production loss so far.
Traction motor capacity of about 1 million electric motors, reusable across customers with tweaks.
Fixed asset turnover fell to 2.9 due to new capitalisation and land purchase; expected to improve as FY26 capex generates revenue in FY27.
ROCE dipped due to fresh equity raised in September 2024; expected to improve over medium term as railway capital is deployed.
demand_pricing: Q4 wins: 4 driveline orders, including 3 from European OEMs (highest ever in a quarter from Europe, first EV win from Europe in about 4 years) and 1 hybrid platform.
FY26: 31 new programs won and 3 new customers added; order book roughly flat YoY after a Q2 correction tied to one model.
Pricing: company says a large part of commodity inflation is passed through with a lag; the remainder hits margins.
Demand: management cites March 2026 BEV sales up about 45% in EU and India e-car and e-2W up 65% and 45%; April trending above 50% in India.
US: Section 232 tariffs (25%) unchanged; management says revenue and margins from US not materially affected.
China: one large Chinese EV customer supplied; management sees entry into China-for-China supply chain as hard for now.

qa_highlights.answer: Management says some opportunities already flowing (recent wins); Europe still a good place to win business over the next 12 months, with no material change to the opportunity set.

qa_highlights.question: Novelic India progress and ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Entity set up in India, launch process started for one customer, SOP at end of calendar 2026 using in-house SMT line. Management declined to give kit value or pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Commodity impact of about 80bps in Q4 – normalising?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: about half mix and half commodity; largely lag in material pass-through. Commodity prices still rising, so margin pressure persists until inflation stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: Suspension motor growth and railway growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Suspension motors to grow 3-4x in volume; traction motors to grow at high double digits. Railway growth over 3-5 years via capacity improvement, white-space variants and new products. No formal growth guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Market size of new railway products?
qa_highlights.answer: HVAC market about ₹2,000-2,500 crore; electric panels about ₹1,500 crore. Full coverage of rolling stock takes 12-15 months for panels and at least 3 years for HVAC.

qa_highlights.question: Margin band and M&A pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin band now 23-25% post railway acquisition. Over 100 M&A opportunities evaluated in 3 years, one acted on; no reportable deal in pipeline.

543300|2026-09.headline: Sona Comstar Q2 FY27 revenue rose 35% YoY to ₹1,546 crore and EBITDA to ₹356 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 23% on mix and input costs.
543300|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 set company records for revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with BEV revenue up 129% YoY and above 50% of automotive revenue for the first time. Margins were lower YoY: EBITDA margin 23% (down 2.3 pp) on traction motor mix shift and West Asia-linked input inflation. Order additions of ₹36 billion (third highest quarter) took the net order book to ₹251 billion, the second highest ever. Management kept the 23-25% EBITDA margin range and flagged the Denso JV closings (JV1 targeted by end-December 2026, JV2 in 1H CY2027).

segments.name: BEV / EV business
segments.commentary: BEV revenue grew 129% YoY and 40% QoQ, and was 51% of automotive product sales in Q2; H1 BEV revenue ₹1,042 crore (+119%). Two-wheeler and three-wheeler demand in India was the main driver.

segments.name: Traction motors
segments.commentary: Business grew about 50% QoQ, faster than management expected; driven by both wallet-share gains at existing OEMs and market growth, and it is the main reason for the margin dilution.

segments.name: EV suspension motors
segments.commentary: Fastest-growing product, reported at about 7% of revenue; its order book so far is with a single customer, with other OEM talks ongoing.

segments.name: Differential assemblies and gears (DA + DG)
segments.commentary: Combined revenue up 37% YoY; all three large EV DA customers picked up in Q2. Entered ICE passenger-car differential assembly with an existing gear customer.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Air springs supplied for the first time this quarter and ramping; first batch of HVAC systems supplied in FY27; electric panels in early ramp-up.

segments.name: Geography and mix
segments.commentary: Eastern markets are about 2/3 of revenue, up from about 1/3 two years ago. Two/three-wheelers are 14% of revenue; auto vs non-auto split 70:30.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin range of 23-25% retained for now; management expects about 23% in a normal macro scenario and says it will hold unless oil reaches about $150.
Margin direction depends on traction motor mix (lower-margin product) and on whether material prices stay high, flat or fall.
JV1 (carve-out of business) targeted to close by end-December 2026, possibly slipping into January 2027; JV2 not yet formed, targeted for 1H CY2027.
Management reiterated a long-term aspiration implying about 25% revenue CAGR, targeting 10x growth over 10 years under Sona Comstar 2.0.

Net cash could reach roughly ₹2,800-3,000 crore by year end if the Denso JV proceeds of about ₹900 crore are received, per analyst arithmetic; management said tax, capex and JV2 capex will absorb part of this.
M&A remains selective; cash-to-EBITDA ratio ceiling of about 1.5x is the stated threshold before deploying cash.
capex_capacity: ₹62 crore of capex declared last quarter for robotics and physical AI, per management.
Helical limited slip differential, air springs for railways and rear radar sensor for two-wheelers commercialised in Q2; three new products in the quarter, a record.

Capacity and capability to ramp fast were cited in the context of traction motor demand; heavy rare earth magnets are unavailable due to Chinese export restrictions, and the company moved to light rare earth alternatives.
AMRs developed in-house are being deployed on Sona factory floors for use-case development.
Robotics and physical AI order book about 4% of the ₹251 billion total order book.
demand_pricing: Q2 order additions ₹36 billion, the third highest quarter; net order book ₹251 billion, the second highest in company history; wins spread across differentials, gears, traction motors, controllers, starter motors, sensors and railways.
Four new EPIC programs in Q2 (3 BEV, 1 intelligent and connected); 75 EPIC programs across 37 customers at end-H1, of which 44 are in production and 31 yet to start.
Inflation: steel, copper and oil derivatives rose on West Asia conflict; freight rates nearly doubled QoQ.
Pass-through contracts exist with customers but lag the input cost increases, and the percentage margin falls arithmetically when costs rise and are passed through.
Europe: OEMs seeking an alternative supply chain to China, and the company is winning more European business.
Management said it is not taking customer-specific questions.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the suspension motor growth, and what is the order pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the product's trajectory is hard to predict; the first launch customer's model underperformed then its new model exceeded expectations. Order book is still limited to one customer, with significant talks with other OEMs; no quantified pipeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Denso JV timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: JV1 (carve-out) targeted to close by end-December 2026, possibly January 2027. JV2 not yet formed, targeted for 1H CY2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why is traction motor growth above industry growth, and what is the three-wheeler contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited both wallet-share gains and market growth, plus OEM supply-chain difficulties that favoured the company's agility. Three-wheeler contribution was not quantified; a further product launch is planned this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold at 23-25% given mix shift and inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept the 23-25% range. CFO said about 23% is the ballpark in a normal scenario and product mix is the key determinant; material price flattening would support margins, further sharp increases would hurt.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net cash position and M&A plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross cash ₹1,966 crore, net ₹1,400-1,500 crore. M&A is selective (three deals in the last decade), with four filters: 15-year product life, top 5-10 global position, margin and return accretion, and moral good. Cash-to-EBITDA ceiling of about 1.5x.

qa_highlights.question: Robotics and humanoid R&D spend, timelines and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is in-house, mostly staff time; ₹62 crore capex is earmarked for the area. Management will demonstrate at Bharat Expo in February 2027. No inflection year was forecast; the curve is expected to be steep when it arrives.

Suspension motor growth depends on a single customer so far; other OEM wins still to be secured.
Heavy rare earth export restrictions from China remain in place with no sign of easing.
Denso JV timing could slip (JV1 into January 2027; JV2 not until 1H CY2027).
Management flagged near-term predictability as difficult due to West Asia inflation.
Railway growth outlook not quantified; depends on timely new-product launches.

543306|2026-03.headline: Dodla Dairy Q4 FY26 revenue rose 18% to INR1,074 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 5% as milk procurement costs outran price hikes.
543306|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue hit a record INR1,074 crore (+18.1% YoY) on volume growth, but EBITDA margin compressed to 5% as procurement cost rose to INR41/litre from INR37.4 a year earlier while average milk sales price moved only to INR58.4/litre. Reported Q4 PAT of INR70 crore (6.5% margin) was flattered by about INR39 crore of one-offs; underlying Q4 PAT is about INR40 crore. FY26 adjusted PAT is about INR215 crore (5.2% margin) against reported INR267 crore. Management guides to a gradual 50-100 bps gross margin recovery in FY27 and low-to-mid-teens revenue growth, with procurement relief expected from June.

segments.name: India standalone
segments.commentary: Q4 milk procurement averaged 18.5 lakh litres/day (+13.4% YoY); procurement cost INR41/litre vs INR37.4 a year ago, and average milk sales price INR58.4/litre vs INR57.7 in Q3. Standalone India EBITDA margin for FY26 was about 6-7%, with Q4 described as a cyclical trough.

segments.name: Value-added products (VAP)
segments.commentary: Total VAP INR2,969 million vs INR2,841 million in Q4 FY25; excluding bulk sales, VAP grew 21% YoY. Curd rupee sales were INR230 crore in Q4 and INR845.7 crore in FY26; consolidated VAP realisation was INR60.54/litre.

segments.name: Africa (Uganda and Kenya)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR151 crore (+48% YoY) with liquid milk volume up more than 60%; record quarterly EBITDA of INR18 crore. FY26 EBITDA margin about 11.3% vs 11% in FY25, and FY26 volume about 2.27 lakh litres/day (Uganda about 1.5 lakh, Kenya about 0.9 lakh).

segments.name: OSAM / HR Food (OrgaFeed)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR81.9 crore (+23.2% YoY) with EBITDA INR2.7 crore; FY26 revenue INR214.7 crore and EBITDA INR4.8 crore. Management cites about 21% gross margin, targeting 25%, and a 6-12 month window to converge with company margins.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided to low-to-mid teens, supported by full-year OSAM consolidation, Africa on current trajectory, and 8-9% organic growth in India.
Gross margin to recover 50-100 bps over FY26 levels as procurement normalises and pricing actions take effect.
Effective tax rate to return to 25-27% after favourable ITAT orders in FY26; no further tax-credit impact from Q1 FY27.
Africa to reach 15-18% of consolidated revenue by FY28; Africa volume growth of about 20% targeted, implying about INR600 crore revenue vs about INR500 crore in FY26.

Capital allocation priority: growth capex (Maharashtra, Uganda, regular capex) from internal accruals, then regular dividends, then selective bolt-on acquisitions.
capex_capacity: Maharashtra project (total envelope INR280 crore): INR20 crore spent in FY25, INR86 crore in FY26, and about INR180 crore planned in FY27; commercial operations expected by end FY27.
FY27 standalone capex budget about INR130 crore, including INR65 crore regular capex and about INR7 crore hardware (excluding Maharashtra).
Uganda greenfield: 70 acres acquired, total capex about INR60 crore including land and plant, phased, completion by end FY29; Phase 2 adds pasteurised milk and milk products.
Bihar: 7-acre land allotted by BIADA for a dairy, with about INR4.4 crore land cost; subject to Board approval.
Maharashtra procurement averages about 3 lakh litres/day, with a target of at least 5 lakh litres/day by end of the season (around end of FY27).
demand_pricing: Company raised prices in mid-March 2026; cooperatives (Amul, Mother Dairy) followed with about INR2/litre hikes in May. Management says the next price action depends on fuel, packaging and freight stabilising, with only minor corrections planned in the near term.
Packaging material costs are up about 30% YoY (mainly plastics); expected to stay elevated as government excise support is temporary.
Freight: fuel up about INR3 recently; management said it will absorb for 15-30 days before passing on, with an estimated impact of about 0.25-0.5%.
Milk volume growth guided at 5-6% for liquid milk (about 9.4% including VAP in FY26); VAP growing 16-17% in the current season.
Procurement cost in mid-May was unchanged from March levels (INR41 consolidated, +9.7% YoY); the company says it has passed on about INR1/litre of the inflation so far.
Realisations: India milk INR58.25 vs INR56.15 YoY; HR Food milk INR55.7 and VAP INR98.8 vs Dodla India VAP INR64.2 (excluding fat products).
Management expects VAP mix to rise to 32-34% of revenue once expansions stabilise; seasonality in curd, buttermilk and lassi being addressed to extend demand from 2-3 months to about six months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state margin in this environment, and is the structural margin lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described FY27 as a cautious, transition year given fuel, plastic and agri-input uncertainty, and said margins can return to normal afterwards; another analyst confirmed the company expects margins to revert to mean by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is procurement cost today versus the Q4 average, and how much inflation has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Procurement remains near March levels at about INR41/litre (+9.7% YoY consolidated, +9.3% standalone). About INR1/litre of inflation has been recovered so far, with another INR1-1.5 expected from procurement relief.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex breakup, and what were Q4 realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 standalone capex about INR130 crore plus Maharashtra INR180 crore. Q4 consolidated realisation was INR61.19 per litre (INR56.16 for milk), and VAP realisation INR60.54 consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: How is OSAM margin expected to converge, and why did OrgaFeed margins drop?
qa_highlights.answer: OSAM margin improvement expected in 6-12 months via SAP, quality and logistics work, targeting about 25% gross margin. OrgaFeed margins fell from higher maize costs and freight for longer distances, but management says the margin is still about 11%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Africa split by country and EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 volume about 1.8 lakh litres/day (Uganda about 1.45 lakh, Kenya about 35,000); FY26 about 2.27 lakh (Uganda about 1.5 lakh, Kenya about 90,000). EBITDA margin about 11% in FY25 and 11.3% in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How has the price-and-volume mix shifted in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Liquid milk volume grew about 5-6% YoY, VAP about 16%. Management says the company did not raise milk prices to protect market share and wants to keep the gap to cooperatives manageable.

El Nino, drought and fuel price volatility (crude moves cited at USD60-120/barrel) could raise procurement, freight and packaging costs faster than prices can be passed on.

OSAM and OrgaFeed margins are below the company average and depend on the pace of the SAP, logistics and procurement fixes.

EBITDA was INR65 crore (5.4% margin) and PAT INR41 crore, as procurement prices stayed elevated (INR41.3/litre vs INR37.4 a year ago) and price pass-through lagged. Management says the pressure is seasonal rather than structural, and it has since taken a further milk price correction of around 2-2.5% in the ongoing quarter. Africa and VAP delivered strong growth, while Orgafeed margins were under pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Why take only a roughly 2% stake in Sids Farm, and what is the rationale?

543308|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 34.8% YoY to INR 1,075 crore, but EBITDA pre-Ind AS fell 33.5% to INR 131 crore as new hospitals dragged margins.

Management attributed the margin compression to roughly INR 32 crore of EBITDA erosion from newer units (in operation under one year), while mature units held about 28.5-29% margins. PAT fell to INR 33 crore from INR 106 crore a year ago. Management is raising about INR 1,500 crore via QIP to cut net debt, which it says has peaked at INR 3,000-plus crore, and targets net debt to EBITDA of 1-2x from about 1x-3x currently.

543308|2026-06.headline: KIMS Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 35.3% YoY to INR 1,180 crore, with EBITDA pre-Ind AS at INR 222 crore and debt cut to INR 2,570 crore.

543317|2026-03.headline: G R Infra Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 27% YoY to INR2,521 crore, but adjusted EBITDA margin fell to ~11% from 15.5%.
543317|2026-03.overview: Standalone revenue grew 27% YoY to about INR2,521 crore in Q4 FY26 and 17% to INR7,620 crore for FY26, driven by oil and gas and power transmission execution. Margins compressed on higher construction costs, with standalone EBITDA margin at ~10.85% in Q4 versus 17.5% a year earlier, which included a one-time claim of INR47.5 crore. Execution slipped in March owing to a delayed appointed date on one project and geopolitical-driven fuel and bitumen price volatility, with oil and gas revenue of ~INR400-450 crore against an internal expectation of ~INR600 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of ~15% and new order wins of INR20,000-22,000 crore, while order book stands at ~INR26,470 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 inflow mainly BOT or HAM, and how big is the NHAI award pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: NHAI is more focused on BOT, but the company will bid both HAM and BOT; NHAI has an outlook of about INR6 lakh crore, with management expecting 70-80% of that, and awards spread across Q2-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth reach 20% in FY27 and 25-30% in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inflows drive next-year revenue, and it expects at least 15-20% growth in FY27 and about 20% in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will margin improve beyond the 10.5-11% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit, citing geopolitical fuel and bitumen exposure; margin outcome depends on how long the disruption lasts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 execution miss, particularly oil and gas?
qa_highlights.answer: Appointed-date delay on one project and March geopolitical disruption; oil and gas executed about INR400-450 crore versus about INR600 crore expected, slowed by price changes and awaited price-variation clauses.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timing for the Agra-Gwalior BOT and the two HAM appointed dates?

qa_highlights.question: Why is execution rate falling versus order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed land aggregation: piecemeal land raises cost and slows work, and provisional appointed dates led to mobilisation before land was ready. Execution rate to be assumed at current level.

543317|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 32.71% YoY to about INR2,423 crores, while consolidated revenue rose 40% to INR2,784 crores. Margins compressed on higher construction and material costs, with standalone EBITDA margin at 11.02% versus 12.65% a year earlier and group EBITDA margin at 16.8% versus 20%. Management kept FY27 standalone revenue growth guidance at 15-20% despite the 30%+ first-quarter run-rate, citing appointed-date timing for new projects. Order book stands at about INR25,300 crores as of 1 July 2026, with about INR32,000 crores of bids yet to be opened.

Order inflow to date has lagged government pipeline claims for about two years, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance still 15% revenue growth after 32% in Q1, and what about FY28 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 guidance kept at 15-20%; FY28 growth could approach 20%. Margin range 10-11% for now, with possible marginal improvement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of the INR32,000 crore bids yet to open, and is INR20,000-25,000 crore inflow achievable?

qa_highlights.question: Why was other income low in Q1 and what is the InvIT distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: InvIT payment was partly capital repayment, which hits the balance sheet, not P&L. Total other income about INR68 crores, of which INR20 crores from InvIT and INR35 crores other interest. InvIT distribution about INR70 crores in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise and when will they unwind?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly oil and gas receivables; collection expected as projects complete, with the current project finishing around May 2027.

qa_highlights.question: How is raw material inflation handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Bitumen is compensated by government circular over escalation. Diesel is not, and power transmission has no escalation, so margins are impacted in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company pursuing international or Middle East opportunities?
qa_highlights.answer: No international focus for the next 1-2 years; domestic credentials first, with international possibly after about one year.

qa_highlights.question: How will the large equity and InvIT value be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans BOT projects, transmission and logistics to deploy accrued cash at meaningful returns; said it is waiting for suitable opportunities.

543318|2026-03.headline: Clean Science Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 8% QoQ to INR193 crore with 46% EBITDA margin; FY26 standalone revenue fell 12% to about INR796 crore.
543318|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue rose 8% QoQ to about INR193 crore on volume recovery, with EBITDA of INR88 crore (46% margin) and PAT of INR77 crore (40%), but revenue fell 19% YoY. For FY26, standalone revenue declined 12% from INR900 crore to INR796 crore, attributed to loss of an FMCG key account (4-MAP), lower offtake and pricing pressure. Consolidated Q4 revenue rose 14% to about INR246 crore, led by HALS (Clean Fino-Chem), with EBITDA of INR96 crore (33%) and PAT of INR58 crore. Management said Clean Fino-Chem reached its first positive EBITDA (INR7 crore) and that the Hydroquinone/Catechol plant is still stabilising at about 10-15% utilisation.

segments.name: Performance chemicals (standalone)
segments.commentary: Contributed 72% of FY26 standalone revenue. Management cited a rebound in flagship product volumes and a gross margin (RMC 33%) about 2 points better than prior quarters.

segments.name: Pharma-Agro (standalone)
segments.commentary: Contributed 19% of FY26 standalone revenue. The pharma intermediate plant was refurbished for HALS intermediates, and the older pharma intermediate was dropped.

segments.name: FMCG (standalone)
segments.commentary: Contributed the balance 9% of FY26 standalone revenue. A key FMCG account (4-MAP) was lost during the year.

segments.name: HALS (Clean Fino-Chem subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Posted its highest-ever quarterly revenue in Q4 FY26, at over 1,000 tonnes per quarter versus about 350-360 tonnes eight quarters earlier. Blended realisation was about INR460/kg versus INR420-430/kg in Q3; exports rose to about 50% of sales in select products from about 20%. Subsidiary EBITDA margin was about 15% in Q4 versus about 1% in Q3.

guidance_outlook: Performance Chemical 2 (water treatment-related capex) expected to commercialise by September 2026; validation in Q3, initial commercial production in Q4, and a pickup in FY28.
Hydroquinone/Catechol plant expected to reach optimal operations in 1-2 quarters; captive HQ/catechol now replaces imports for TBHQ and Veratrole.
Capex budget for FY27 of about INR80-100 crore; Clean Fino-Chem projects under an INR200 crore enabling Board resolution, with investment likely in the second half of FY27.
Management aspires to a HALS blended realisation of USD7-7.5/kg but did not give FY27 revenue or EBITDA guidance, calling FY27 a 'very tricky' year dependent on macro and crude oil.
Management said it is not pencilling in any price hikes; it expects to benefit in an inflationary environment, as it did in FY23.
capex_capacity: Clean Fino-Chem Hydroquinone/Catechol plant commissioned in December 2025; still in initial stabilisation, with utilisation about 10-15% and March 2026 HALS exit utilisation about 40%.
Performance Chemical 2 commercialisation timeline moved due to scarce manpower linked to labour movement from higher gas prices; now targeted by September 2026.

Q4 other expenses were inflated by about INR22 crore of U.S. customs duty (about half recoverable from customers) and about INR6 crore of one-time legal and professional costs tied to the lender settlement. The company completed the INR101 crore Right of Recompense payment to lenders on March 31, 2026, and announced a INR180 crore buyback at INR180 per share, from which promoters are not participating.

Management said operations normalised from June, July 2026 was the highest-revenue month since inception, and it reiterated mid-teen FY27 revenue growth guidance while cutting its margin guidance to 21-22% citing ocean freight costs.

543330|2026-03.headline: Devyani Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 18.5% YoY to INR 1,437 crore, with KFC SSSG at 4.9%, its best in 14 quarters.
543330|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 18.5% YoY to INR 1,437 crore, and FY26 revenue crossed INR 5,500 crore at INR 5,611 crore. KFC returned to positive SSSG of 4.9% with nearly 15% YoY revenue growth, driven by a shift in focus to dine-in customers and store-level deals. Pizza Hut SSSG stayed negative at -3.7% and brand contribution was slightly negative, while the international business grew 20% YoY. Management is pursuing the Sapphire Foods merger, targeting completion by end of FY27, and is rebuilding the leadership team. Store count was 2,256 at year end, with negative net additions in Q4.

qa_highlights.answer: Management hired Neeraj Tiwari as CTO, Sandeep Anand as CMO (also overseeing Pizza Hut operations), and announced a COO from FMCG and technology backgrounds who joins in the next couple of weeks. Other appointments cover Costa and smaller brands. The aim is in-house technology capability and operational transformation.

543330|2026-06.headline: Devyani Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 16.5% YoY to INR 1,581 crore, with record Operating EBITDA of INR 151 crore (9.6% margin).
543330|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16.5% YoY to INR 1,581 crore and Operating EBITDA rose about 38% YoY to INR 151 crore, the company's highest ever, at a 9.6% margin. KFC returned to positive SSSG (3.3%) with dine-in salience improving to 57%, while Pizza Hut remained loss-making at brand contribution level with SSSG of -2.2%. Management flagged LPG, wage and commodity inflation, a weak monsoon outlook and volatile macro, and said Sapphire merger approvals from NSE and BSE were received in June with completion targeted by end FY27.

segments.name: KFC India
segments.commentary: SSSG +3.3%, revenue INR 684 crore (~+12% YoY), gross margin 69.4%, brand contribution INR 115 crore; offline saliency 57%, up over 3 pp YoY. Management targets 59-60% dine-in share and ADS of 105k-110k for 20%+ brand contribution margin.

segments.name: Pizza Hut
segments.commentary: SSSG -2.2% (improving sequentially), ADS up to ~INR 32,400 per store per day, revenue INR 184 crore, gross margin 76.3%, brand contribution loss INR 4 crore; 626 stores at quarter end.

segments.name: Own brands (BBK, Vaango)
segments.commentary: Biryani By Kilo SSSG +7.2%, Vaango +7.1%; combined revenue INR 98 crore, gross margin 65.9%, brand contribution ~INR 10 crore (10.2%). 218 stores including 23 BBK Express; BBK target INR 1,000 crore brand in next few years.

segments.name: Franchise brands (incl. Costa)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew ~6% YoY; gross margin fell to 74.6% on input costs; brand contribution margin 15.1%, up YoY on cost management.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 523 crore, growth above 20% YoY for another quarter; brand contribution margin 18.2%, up 1.5 pp YoY.

guidance_outlook: KFC SSSG expected around 5-6% over the medium term per management; Percy Panthaki's follow-up framed 105k-110k ADS as roughly 1.5-2 years away on that basis.
Brand contribution margin for KFC to cross 20% once ADS passes 105k-110k; management said this is conditional on the current cost environment.
Store opening plan unchanged from earlier guidance; 11 net new KFC and 3 net new BBK stores in India in Q1; 1,855 stores in India and 2,255 globally at June 30, 2026.

capex_capacity: Store opening pace in line with prior guidance; 11 net new KFC and 3 net new BBK stores in India in Q1.
Management said there is spare capacity in existing KFC stores, so the dine-in shift needs no additional capex; future formats will stay as currently sized.
BBK Express small-box format (23 stores) being tested in food courts; BBK dine-in and airport formats being piloted.
Technology platform build: core team in-house with outsourcing to Cognizant; tech rollout targeted before merger approval.
demand_pricing: KFC SSSG +3.3%; management reports demand 'stable' and July trends positive, but macro (LPG, rupee, crude) remains a constraint.
Slight price increases taken at KFC and Pizza Hut to offset LPG and commodity costs; KFC gross margin restored to 69.4% through judicious discounting.
KFC marketing rebalanced from deep online discounting toward dine-in visits.
Pizza Hut ADS is low versus peers; management says innovation and price laddering across price points are needed, with product work ongoing.
Franchise brands gross margin fell to 74.6% on higher input costs, offset by better cost management.

qa_highlights.question: What drivers beyond SSSG could lift KFC margins from ~17% and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the key lever is ADS; crossing 105k-110k ADS should take KFC brand contribution above 20%. Other levers are dine-in promotion, operating leverage and technology adoption, which will only deliver a few quarters after the merger.

qa_highlights.question: Can KFC dine-in salience return to 60-65%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 65% is not achievable near term given convenience preference, especially in the North; the target is 59-60%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is SSSG not guided higher after 13 quarters of negative trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited tough macro (rupee, oil, LPG availability) and said a bullish view needs a stable environment that it does not yet see.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for Pizza Hut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 3-way structure with Sapphire and Yum! held back decisions and innovation; product, ingredient and price-ladder work is underway, with full push after the merger.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mandate and leadership build-out?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoters are supportive on investment; new COO, CTO and CMO have been hired, with joinings ranging from 2 weeks to 2 months; the whole leadership team is now in place.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Sapphire integration be straightforward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IT stacks and processes are largely similar because technology was run by Yum!, so integration should not be a major challenge.

risks_watch: Inflation in LPG, wages, food commodities and packaging could offset the KFC margin path; management said the ADS target may move if costs rise.
Below-normal monsoon forecast and El Niño risk could weigh on demand.
Pizza Hut remains loss-making at brand contribution level with ADS well below peers.
Merger completion by end FY27 and the technology build-out being ready before merger approval.
Aggregator dynamics and delivery cannibalising dine-in sales; management is shifting marketing toward dine-in.

543331|2026-03.headline: Meghmani Organics FY26 standalone revenue rose 4% to INR 2,091 crore and EBITDA 27% to INR 228.7 crore, but Q4 standalone EBITDA was only INR 26.2 crore.
543331|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a difficult year: US tariffs, a weaker export environment and the US-Iran war pushed raw material costs up while realisations stayed broadly flat. Standalone EBITDA recovered 27% for the full year, but Q4 remained thin, with Crop Protection margin near 9% and Pigments near 3%. Management suspended TiO2 operations as unviable after the anti-dumping duty was withdrawn and sulphuric acid prices spiked. Management guided to Crop Protection margins of 15-17% in FY27, double-digit Crop Protection top-line growth, and a Nano fertiliser ramp-up, and announced an amalgamation of two subsidiaries and a Brazil subsidiary.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA up 24% YoY; margin vs 6.9% prior year

segments.name: Crop Protection (FY26)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,631 crore (about 78% of standalone revenue), EBITDA INR 244 crore, margin 15%; production about 40,371 MT at about 72% utilisation. Q4 revenue INR 348.6 crore, EBITDA INR 31.3 crore, margin about 9%.

segments.name: Pigments (FY26)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 461 crore (about 22% of revenue), EBITDA INR 15 crore, margin 3.3%; production about 13,191 MT at 40% utilisation. Q4 revenue INR 108 crore, EBITDA INR 3.2 crore, margin about 3%.

segments.name: Crop Nutrition
segments.commentary: Nano fertiliser products (Nano DAP, Nano NPK, Nano Zinc) received Ministry of Agriculture approval, to be made at Sanand, Gujarat with no additional capex. Commercial production expected in the Kharif season; Nano Urea is the key product, with about 7-8 products in the basket. No segment financials disclosed.

segments.name: Titanium Dioxide (Kilburn)
segments.commentary: Operations temporarily suspended as commercially unviable after the anti-dumping duty withdrawal, higher sulphuric acid and utility costs. Anti-dumping matter is under DGTR review.

guidance_outlook: Crop Protection: management expects EBITDA margin within 15-17% in FY27, and double-digit top-line growth with better profitability than Q4.
Pigments: top line of about INR 500-600 crore; FY27 profitability expected to be better than FY26's 3.3% margin, though not dramatically so.
Crop Nutrition: significant growth in top line and bottom line over the next 2-5 years; management declined to give quarter-wise timing and said FY27 as a whole will show growth.
Capex: no significant capex in FY27; routine capex of INR 35-40 crore. Working capital to improve through inventory and receivable-day reduction.
Dividend: management said it will try to provide a reasonably good dividend in FY27, subject to Board approval.
Renewable energy: 3.3 MW wind-solar hybrid power agreement, taking renewable share of energy use above 50%.

qa_highlights.answer: No dividend was declared for FY26; management said it will try to provide a reasonably good dividend in FY27, subject to Board approval, based on better revenue and profitability.

qa_highlights.question: When will the TiO2 anti-dumping duty be restored and when will sulphuric acid prices stabilise?

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined quarter-wise guidance, saying some orders will come in Q1 and Q2 and the full year will show significant growth; it confirmed existing orders and expects more.

qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give sell-out data. It said IFFCO has the upper hand due to conventional urea presence, and Meghmani's Nano product basket is being expanded.

543332|2026-03.headline: Epigral posted record Q4 FY26 revenue of INR736 crore (+22% QoQ) and 23% EBITDA margin; management guides FY27 volume growth of 10-12%.

EBITDA rose 64% QoQ to INR169 crore, margin 23%, and PAT was INR82 crore (11% margin). FY26 revenue fell 1% to INR2,542 crore on a ~4% volume decline; reported PAT of INR330 crore includes an INR81 crore one-time deferred tax benefit, so underlying PAT was INR252 crore versus INR357 crore. Management said the war-driven price spike mostly lands in Q1 FY27, not Q4, and the company is targeting 10-12% volume growth in FY27.

543336|2026-03.headline: Chemplast Q4 FY26 net loss of INR45 crores on INR898 crore CCVL impairment; consolidated EBITDA rose to INR194 crores from INR37 crores.

Management said suspension PVC spreads are at roughly breakeven on a replacement-cost basis because of Chinese carbide PVC imports, while specialty chemicals grew 13%. The Board also formed a committee of three independent directors to review strategic priorities, reorganisation and M&A.

Specialty chemicals (CMCD) volumes grew 21% YoY and the segment is described as recovering, while Suspension PVC and caustic/chloromethane remained under price pressure. rows.why: Management is confident of beating its INR1,000 crore CDMO revenue target, with four validated CDMO products contributing from H2 FY27 at INR50-100 crore peak each, but no revised numbers were given and Q1 revenue growth of 59.1% YoY is well above the 25% FY27 guide.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gulf geopolitical tensions have hit raw material supply, working capital days rose to 99 from 91, and CDMO revenue concentration rose on one anchor product, though guidance was reiterated.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Four validated CDMO products expected to contribute from H2 FY27 at INR50-100 crore peak each per year; electrolyte additives Phase 2 (third product) completes end Q2 FY27 with trial runs after; Caplyta-related generic awaiting launch after DMF filed.

rows.label: Battery chemicals supply contracts and demand constrained by capacity
rows.why: Supply contracts are in place with multiple customers across North America, Korea and other regions, and management says demand is constrained by plant capacity, not demand; no revenue quantified.

rows.label: Indichem Korea revenue
rows.why: Plant capex expected complete by end Q1 FY27 and ahead of schedule, with revenue guided from FY28 onwards, but no commercial timeline for new products and margin withheld.

tone.note: Management was confident on 25% FY27 revenue growth, stable margins, battery demand and CDMO INR1,000 crore target, but evasive on battery revenue, CDMO split, Indichem margins and five-year margin outlook; analysts pushed on these specifics.

543349|2026-09.headline: Acutaas Q2 FY27 revenue rose 42.7% YoY to Rs 4,369 mn with EBITDA margin at 40.3%; FY27 revenue growth guidance raised to ~30%.
543349|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations grew 42.7% YoY to Rs 4,369 mn in Q2 FY27, driven by the Advanced Pharmaceutical Intermediate segment (Rs 4,020 mn, up 53.1%), while Specialty Chemicals fell 20% YoY to Rs 349 mn. Gross margin expanded 637 bps to 62.1% and EBITDA margin to 40.3% (up 914 bps), with PAT up 71.4% to Rs 1,231 mn. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance from 25% to about 30% and EBITDA margin guidance to 38-40%, and reaffirmed the CDMO target of Rs 1,000 mn... crores (Rs 1,000 crore) for FY27 and Rs 2,000 crore by FY30. Working capital days rose to 115 from 99 in Q1 on higher debtor days.

segments.name: Advanced Pharmaceutical Intermediates
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 4,020 mn in Q2 FY27, up 53.1% YoY; core pharma business grew more than 25% YoY. New CDMO contracts expected to contribute from H2 FY27. Management does not split CDMO from base business.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 349 mn, down 20% YoY due to phase-out of legacy commodity products and a temporary BFC shipment pause after a change in ownership of a U.S. customer; shipments have resumed.

segments.name: Battery Chemicals
segments.commentary: First quarter of commercial revenue. VC and FEC commercial supply started, third product dispatched in the quarter; fourth product at pilot-scale validation. Revenue not disclosed; ramp expected over next 2-3 quarters.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance raised to around 30% from 25%.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance raised to 38-40%; management confirmed this applies to FY27 only, not FY28.
CDMO revenue expected to cross Rs 1,000 crore in FY27, one year ahead of the FY28 target set in Jan 2025.
CDMO revenue target of Rs 2,000 crore by FY30; CDMO EBITDA margin expected in the same range as current CDMO margins.

Full-year FY27 capex about Rs 3,000 mn; H2 FY27 capex about Rs 1,650 mn (about Rs 1,000 mn electronic-grade chemicals, Rs 450 mn electrolyte additive phase 2, rest maintenance), excluding R&D capex and land acquisition.
Electronic-grade bulk chemicals plant expected to start production in H1 FY29.
Legacy Paraben and MS products to scale down over about 1-1.5 years; MS may take longer.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex Rs 1,239 mn across electrolyte additive project, pilot plant, Indicam site and maintenance.
Ankleshwar Unit 2 (CDMO): Rs 330 crore invested; utilisation 30% in Q2 FY27, expected to be no more than about 40% by end FY27; largely filled by FY28.
Indicam plant in South Korea inaugurated ahead of schedule; FY28 expected to be a ramp-up year for initial semiconductor products.
Next CDMO capex round deferred; land acquisition being planned first, with size to be decided later.
Battery chemicals plant utilisation described as very low at present.
demand_pricing: Pharma intermediate demand described as robust; cost pressures from geopolitical issues passed on to customers.
Several large generic products going off-patent; company has pre-developed intermediates for them.
Battery chemicals: industry demand exceeds supply; company cites strong order book.

Electrolyte additive pricing under long-term contracts linked to raw material and FX movements; management said realisations will be in the early teens (USD/kg basis implied) rather than the USD 30-35 spot levels cited by an analyst.
Management declined to say whether gross margin gain came from raw-material softening; said raw material prices had not softened in the quarter.
CDMO projects are all with originators, no generics; 8-10 products in pipeline; non-blockbuster products typically Rs 50-100 crore each.
Semiconductor customers targeted are in Korea, Japan and the U.S.; Indian ecosystem not yet mature.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue expected from new CDMO products in FY27, and their contribution to the Rs 2,000 crore FY30 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not give product-wise revenue; FY27 Rs 1,000 crore CDMO target is backed by orders on already-validated products. Around 8-9 products to enter revenue over the next 1-1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for battery, semiconductor and electronic-grade chemical revenues?
qa_highlights.answer: Battery products already contributing; electronic-grade bulk chemical plant takes about 1.5 years to build, so production from H1 FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Electrolyte realisations versus recent price spike?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term supply contracts with raw material and FX-linked pricing; management says realisations can be early teens, not USD 30-35, and it does not chase price waves.

qa_highlights.question: Will Darolutamide volumes double from the same facility, and does Ankleshwar need capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation is about 30% with room available; would not disclose wallet share or whether further capex is needed. It cannot comment on the product's market or indication expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Korea semiconductor facility: initial economics and target markets?
qa_highlights.answer: No tall commitment for FY28; revenue will be small initially with sample and pilot dispatches under way. Targets are photoresist and fab customers in Korea and Japan, not cell makers.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin guidance of 38-40% continue into FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is for FY27 only; the margin uplift is attributed to CDMO mix and to operating leverage as Unit 2 and battery plants scale.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin expansion to 62.1%: how much is raw material versus mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot split the gain between raw material and mix; both contributed, and raw material prices did not soften in the quarter.

risks_watch: Specialty Chemicals revenue declined 20% YoY and remains a drag until legacy Paraben/MS exits and battery and BFC ramp up.
CDMO concentration: Darolutamide-linked volumes are a key driver, and management declined to discuss customer or product-level detail.
Working capital days rose to 115 from 99 in Q1 on higher debtor days.
Electronic-grade plant (H1 FY29) and Korea semiconductor ramp carry execution and qualification risk; management flagged geopolitical, supply chain, power and water constraints.
Margin guidance of 38-40% is for FY27 only; sustainability into FY28 is not guided.
543349|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth and guidance upgrades, with a strong focus on CDMO visibility. Management was evasive and declined to give product, customer, split, or wallet-share detail on CDMO, Darolutamide, and the pharma base business, and on battery revenue.
key_quotes: Based on the current orders of existing as well as new CDMO contracts, we now believe we will achieve this target one year ahead of schedule.
Before I conclude, I would also like to revise our revenue growth guidance for current year from 25% to around 30%.
So we are not riding on some of the waves wherein price fluctuation, we don't want to get benefits from those price fluctuations or when it gets down.

rows.why: Specialty Chemicals fell 20% YoY to Rs 349 mn, working capital days rose to 115 from 99, and FY28 margin is not guided, while battery utilisation is described as very low and the Korea ramp carries qualification risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Around 8-9 CDMO products to enter revenue over the next 1-1.5 years, the fourth battery product is at pilot-scale validation, and the Korea semiconductor ramp starts in FY28.

rows.why: Third battery product dispatched in Q2 with VC and FEC commercial supply started, and management cites industry demand exceeding supply and a strong order book, though revenue is undisclosed and plant utilisation is very low.
